```rust
//! sim-emit: the NCU-metric emission layer (design §6.4).
//!
//! Takes a completed kernel replay's counter snapshot and produces a typed
//! vector of NCU metric PREDICTIONS, one per registry observation contract
//! (`tools/local_labels/metric_registry.json`). It is the ONLY sim crate that
//! names label-pipeline contracts: metric NAMES are the output contract and
//! are allowed here; label VALUES still never enter (Rule 1, enforced by
//! `eval/guards/test_targets_not_features_guard.py`).
//!
//! Shape (design proposal P3, "descriptor-table hybrid"): a compiled
//! [`DESCRIPTORS`] table is the single source of truth — one row per emitted
//! metric binds a registry key + NCU metric string + [`Unit`] + [`MetricKind`]
//! to a pure emit fn over the raw counters. A registry-lockstep test walks the
//! table against `metric_registry.json` so a descriptor can never drift from
//! the contract it claims to implement. Rate accounting lives HERE, never in
//! the cache counter structs (gate-2 altitude note c): `L1Counters`/
//! `L2Counters` hold raw counts; the emit fns compose them.
//!
//! Three states are kept distinct, never conflated into a silent zero:
//!   * a real zero — `Exact(0)` / `Fraction { value: Some(0.0), .. }`
//!     (accesses happened, none hit);
//!   * not-applicable — `Fraction { value: None, denominator: 0, .. }`
//!     (no accesses; NCU reports n/a — a legitimate scorable prediction);
//!   * not-produced-by-this-run — [`EmitOutcome::Unavailable`] (the replay's
//!     mem-mode lacks the counting unit, e.g. no L2 under `L1Const`).
//!
//! LDGSTS folding (the §6.4 op_ld surface): NCU books LDGSTS (cp.async) global
//! loads under `op_ld` on the frozen sm_86 bundle — verified against the
//! bundle's own captured counts, NOT the metric-name taxonomy (a witness
//! kernel with only LDGSTS loads and no ordinary loads shows all of its
//! `op_ld` requests attributed to the async copies, with the total-request
//! rollup balancing exactly against `op_ld` + `op_st`). So the op_ld surface
//! folds the READ-class bypass stream (`bypass_sectors - bypass_atom_sectors`,
//! the async-copy loads) into its denominator; the ATOM write-class subset
//! stays out (NCU books it under op_atom/op_red). The sim models LDGSTS as
//! pure bypass with no L1 residency, so those sectors contribute to the
//! denominator but never to the hit numerator — an honest v0 under-prediction
//! whose residual localizes the un-modeled LDGSTS-L1-residency effect.

use sim_mem::{L1Counters, L2Counters};
use sim_sm::{DramStats, KernelReplayResult};

/// The exact counter fields the emission layer reads, borrowed. Decouples
/// emission from the full `KernelReplayResult` so a cell's counters — summed
/// across its kernel launches — can be emitted directly (rates compose from
/// summed numerators/denominators; they cannot be averaged post-hoc).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct CounterSnapshot<'a> {
    /// `smsp__inst_executed.sum` source — total warp-instructions issued.
    pub instructions_issued: u64,
    /// L1TEX counters, present iff the replay attached an L1 (not `Flat`).
    pub l1: Option<&'a L1Counters>,
    /// L2 counters, present only on the shared-L2 path.
    pub l2: Option<&'a L2Counters>,
    /// DRAM read observer, present only on the shared-L2 path.
    pub dram: Option<&'a DramStats>,
}

impl<'a> CounterSnapshot<'a> {
    /// Borrow the emission-relevant counters out of one completed replay.
    pub fn from_replay(r: &'a KernelReplayResult) -> Self {
        Self {
            instructions_issued: r.instructions_issued,
            l1: r.l1.as_ref(),
            l2: r.l2.as_ref(),
            dram: r.dram.as_ref(),
        }
    }
}

/// A predicted metric value, shaped to its NCU contract. The numeric payload
/// carries num/den so a `None` rate is auditable in-band (None IFF den == 0).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub enum MetricValue {
    /// An exact non-negative integer count (sectors, requests, instructions).
    Exact(u64),
    /// A `[0, 1]` fraction. `value` is `None` iff `denominator == 0` (NCU
    /// reports the metric as n/a — never a fabricated 0.0).
    Fraction {
        value: Option<f64>,
        numerator: u64,
        denominator: u64,
    },
}

impl MetricValue {
    /// Fail-closed `[0, 1]` fraction constructor. `value` is `None` iff
    /// `den == 0`; a `num > den` fraction is a counter-arithmetic bug and is
    /// surfaced typed, never clamped into range.
    fn fraction(key: &'static str, num: u64, den: u64) -> Result<Self, EmitError> {
        if num > den {
            return Err(EmitError::RateExceedsUnity { key, num, den });
        }
        Ok(Self::Fraction {
            value: (den != 0).then(|| num as f64 / den as f64),
            numerator: num,
            denominator: den,
        })
    }
}

/// The NCU-facing unit of a metric (the registry `unit` field). Only the
/// variants v0 uses are declared; cycles/ns/ratio arrive with their metrics.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Unit {
    /// A raw non-negative count.
    Count,
    /// A percentage in NCU's own rendering; stored as a `[0, 1]` fraction
    /// (registry `parser_transform = percent_to_fraction`).
    Pct,
}

/// The numeric shape a descriptor promises to emit — asserted against the
/// returned [`MetricValue`] so a wrong-variant slip fails loudly, and pinned
/// against the registry `metric_class`/`valid_max` by the lockstep test.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MetricKind {
    /// Emits [`MetricValue::Exact`].
    Count,
    /// Emits [`MetricValue::Fraction`].
    Fraction,
}

/// A hardware counting unit a metric needs to be predictable at all.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MemUnit {
    /// The L1TEX cache (`KernelReplayResult.l1`).
    L1Tex,
    /// The L2 slices (`KernelReplayResult.l2`).
    Lts,
    /// The DRAM read observer (`KernelReplayResult.dram`).
    Dram,
}

/// Typed reason a metric was NOT predicted by THIS run — distinct from a
/// value-level `None` (which means "predicted n/a: no accesses"). The harness
/// excludes such a cell with a reason rather than scoring a null.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Unavailable {
    /// The replay's mem-mode did not attach the counting unit this metric
    /// reads (e.g. no L2 counters under `Flat`/`L1Const`).
    MemModeLacksUnit { needs: MemUnit },
}

/// Per-metric outcome: a genuine prediction, or a typed not-produced reason.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub enum EmitOutcome {
    Predicted(MetricValue),
    Unavailable(Unavailable),
}

/// One emitted metric, carrying its registry key + NCU identifier so the eval
/// join (downstream, outside `sim/`) can match against frozen labels by key.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub struct MetricPrediction {
    /// The registry key — the eval JOIN key.
    pub key: &'static str,
    /// The NCU metric identifier this predicts.
    pub ncu_metric: &'static str,
    pub unit: Unit,
    pub outcome: EmitOutcome,
}

/// A compiled row of the emission table: the binding from a sim quantity to
/// its registry contract. [`DESCRIPTORS`] is the single source of truth the
/// lockstep test pins against `metric_registry.json`.
pub struct MetricDescriptor {
    pub key: &'static str,
    pub ncu_metric: &'static str,
    pub unit: Unit,
    pub kind: MetricKind,
    pub emit: fn(&CounterSnapshot) -> Result<EmitOutcome, EmitError>,
}

/// Fail-closed emission faults. Benign "this run's mem-mode lacks the unit" is
/// NOT an error — it is an [`Unavailable`] outcome inside the vector, so a
/// Flat-mode run still emits the instruction count while marking the cache
/// rates typed-unavailable (the Carded::Gap / unsupported_memory_path idiom).
#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum EmitError {
    #[error(
        "metric {key}: rate numerator {num} exceeds denominator {den} — a >1.0 fraction is a \
         counter bug, never clamped into range"
    )]
    RateExceedsUnity {
        key: &'static str,
        num: u64,
        den: u64,
    },
    #[error("counter invariant broken for {key}: {detail}")]
    CounterInvariant {
        key: &'static str,
        detail: &'static str,
    },
}

/// READ-class bypass sectors = all bypass sectors minus the ATOM write-class
/// subset. This is the LDGSTS/bypass-LOAD stream that folds into the `op_ld`
/// surface; the ATOM subset (booked under op_atom/op_red by NCU) stays out.
fn bypass_read_sectors(key: &'static str, l1: &L1Counters) -> Result<u64, EmitError> {
    l1.bypass_sectors
        .checked_sub(l1.bypass_atom_sectors)
        .ok_or(EmitError::CounterInvariant {
            key,
            detail: "bypass_atom_sectors exceeds bypass_sectors (subset invariant broken)",
        })
}

// ---- per-metric emit fns (the rate accounting, moved out of the counters) ----

/// `smsp__inst_executed.sum` — total warp-instructions issued. One issue per
/// traced record across every SM; always available (no mem unit needed).
fn emit_smsp_inst_executed(snap: &CounterSnapshot) -> Result<EmitOutcome, EmitError> {
    Ok(EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::Exact(
        snap.instructions_issued,
    )))
}

/// `l1tex__t_sectors_pipe_lsu_mem_global_op_ld.sum` — global-load sectors:
/// modeled eligible loads plus the READ-class bypass (LDGSTS) stream.
fn emit_gmem_ld_sectors(snap: &CounterSnapshot) -> Result<EmitOutcome, EmitError> {
    let key = "traffic_gmem_ld_sectors";
    let Some(l1) = snap.l1 else {
        return Ok(EmitOutcome::Unavailable(Unavailable::MemModeLacksUnit {
            needs: MemUnit::L1Tex,
        }));
    };
    let sectors = l1.hits + l1.misses + bypass_read_sectors(key, l1)?;
    Ok(EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::Exact(sectors)))
}

/// `l1tex__t_sectors_pipe_lsu_mem_global_op_st.sum` — global-store sectors.
fn emit_gmem_st_sectors(snap: &CounterSnapshot) -> Result<EmitOutcome, EmitError> {
    let Some(l1) = snap.l1 else {
        return Ok(EmitOutcome::Unavailable(Unavailable::MemModeLacksUnit {
            needs: MemUnit::L1Tex,
        }));
    };
    Ok(EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::Exact(l1.store_sectors)))
}

/// `l1tex__t_sector_pipe_lsu_mem_global_op_ld_hit_rate.pct` — the op_ld sector
/// hit rate. Numerator = modeled eligible hits; denominator folds the
/// READ-class bypass (LDGSTS) sectors in (they miss L1 structurally in v0, so
/// they enter the denominator but contribute no hits — the honest residual).
fn emit_l1tex_read_hit_rate(snap: &CounterSnapshot) -> Result<EmitOutcome, EmitError> {
    let key = "cache_hit_rate_l1tex_read_sector";
    let Some(l1) = snap.l1 else {
        return Ok(EmitOutcome::Unavailable(Unavailable::MemModeLacksUnit {
            needs: MemUnit::L1Tex,
        }));
    };
    let num = l1.hits;
    let den = l1.hits + l1.misses + bypass_read_sectors(key, l1)?;
    Ok(EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::fraction(
        key, num, den,
    )?))
}

/// `l1tex__t_sector_hit_rate.pct` — the unified L1TEX sector hit rate over all
/// op classes. v0 numerator uses the sector-valid store rule (`store_hits`);
/// the §6.4 line-TAG rule (`store_tag_hits`) is the carried alternative,
/// unresolved until l1tex store accounting is scored. The full bypass stream
/// (atom included) is in the denominator — the unified metric covers
/// global_atomic/global_reduction, so `bypass_atom_sectors` must NOT be added
/// on top (it is already a subset of `bypass_sectors`).
fn emit_l1tex_unified_hit_rate(snap: &CounterSnapshot) -> Result<EmitOutcome, EmitError> {
    let key = "cache_hit_rate_l1tex_sector";
    let Some(l1) = snap.l1 else {
        return Ok(EmitOutcome::Unavailable(Unavailable::MemModeLacksUnit {
            needs: MemUnit::L1Tex,
        }));
    };
    let num = l1.hits + l1.store_hits;
    let den = l1.hits + l1.misses + l1.store_sectors + l1.bypass_sectors + l1.untagged_sectors;
    Ok(EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::fraction(
        key, num, den,
    )?))
}

/// `lts__t_sector_hit_rate.pct` — the unified L2 sector hit rate. Every LTS
/// access from all four L2 source lanes is in `l2.hits`/`l2.misses`;
/// `write_tag_hits` is already a subset of `hits` (do not add it).
fn emit_l2_hit_rate(snap: &CounterSnapshot) -> Result<EmitOutcome, EmitError> {
    let key = "cache_hit_rate_l2_sector";
    let Some(l2) = snap.l2 else {
        return Ok(EmitOutcome::Unavailable(Unavailable::MemModeLacksUnit {
            needs: MemUnit::Lts,
        }));
    };
    Ok(EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::fraction(
        key,
        l2.hits,
        l2.total(),
    )?))
}

/// `dram__sectors_read.sum` — DRAM read sectors (v0 read-only demand proxy).
fn emit_dram_read_sectors(snap: &CounterSnapshot) -> Result<EmitOutcome, EmitError> {
    let Some(dram) = snap.dram else {
        return Ok(EmitOutcome::Unavailable(Unavailable::MemModeLacksUnit {
            needs: MemUnit::Dram,
        }));
    };
    Ok(EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::Exact(
        dram.read_sectors,
    )))
}

/// The v0 emission table — one row per registry contract this layer predicts.
/// Adding a metric is a one-row append plus its emit fn; the lockstep test and
/// the eval join need no edits.
pub const DESCRIPTORS: &[MetricDescriptor] = &[
    MetricDescriptor {
        key: "smsp_inst_executed_sum",
        ncu_metric: "smsp__inst_executed.sum",
        unit: Unit::Count,
        kind: MetricKind::Count,
        emit: emit_smsp_inst_executed,
    },
    MetricDescriptor {
        key: "traffic_gmem_ld_sectors",
        ncu_metric: "l1tex__t_sectors_pipe_lsu_mem_global_op_ld.sum",
        unit: Unit::Count,
        kind: MetricKind::Count,
        emit: emit_gmem_ld_sectors,
    },
    MetricDescriptor {
        key: "traffic_gmem_st_sectors",
        ncu_metric: "l1tex__t_sectors_pipe_lsu_mem_global_op_st.sum",
        unit: Unit::Count,
        kind: MetricKind::Count,
        emit: emit_gmem_st_sectors,
    },
    MetricDescriptor {
        key: "cache_hit_rate_l1tex_read_sector",
        ncu_metric: "l1tex__t_sector_pipe_lsu_mem_global_op_ld_hit_rate.pct",
        unit: Unit::Pct,
        kind: MetricKind::Fraction,
        emit: emit_l1tex_read_hit_rate,
    },
    MetricDescriptor {
        key: "cache_hit_rate_l1tex_sector",
        ncu_metric: "l1tex__t_sector_hit_rate.pct",
        unit: Unit::Pct,
        kind: MetricKind::Fraction,
        emit: emit_l1tex_unified_hit_rate,
    },
    MetricDescriptor {
        key: "cache_hit_rate_l2_sector",
        ncu_metric: "lts__t_sector_hit_rate.pct",
        unit: Unit::Pct,
        kind: MetricKind::Fraction,
        emit: emit_l2_hit_rate,
    },
    MetricDescriptor {
        key: "traffic_dram_read_sectors",
        ncu_metric: "dram__sectors_read.sum",
        unit: Unit::Count,
        kind: MetricKind::Count,
        emit: emit_dram_read_sectors,
    },
];

/// Assert an emit fn returned the numeric shape its descriptor promised.
fn shape_matches(kind: MetricKind, value: &MetricValue) -> bool {
    matches!(
        (kind, value),
        (MetricKind::Count, MetricValue::Exact(_))
            | (MetricKind::Fraction, MetricValue::Fraction { .. })
    )
}

/// Emit every descriptor over one completed replay, in registry-table order.
/// Genuine faults (a rate above unity, a broken subset invariant) return
/// [`EmitError`]; benign missing-unit cases ride the [`Unavailable`] arm.
pub fn emit_all(snap: &CounterSnapshot) -> Result<Vec<MetricPrediction>, EmitError> {
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(DESCRIPTORS.len());
    for d in DESCRIPTORS {
        let outcome = (d.emit)(snap)?;
        if let EmitOutcome::Predicted(v) = &outcome {
            debug_assert!(
                shape_matches(d.kind, v),
                "emit fn for {} returned a value shape inconsistent with its declared kind",
                d.key
            );
        }
        out.push(MetricPrediction {
            key: d.key,
            ncu_metric: d.ncu_metric,
            unit: d.unit,
            outcome,
        });
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// A by-key view of a prediction vector for the eval join.
pub fn index_by_key(
    preds: &[MetricPrediction],
) -> std::collections::BTreeMap<&'static str, &MetricPrediction> {
    preds.iter().map(|p| (p.key, p)).collect()
}

#[cfg(test)]
#[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use sim_mem::{L1Counters, L2Counters};
    use sim_sm::DramStats;

    /// A replay result carrying just the counters the emit fns read.
    fn replay(
        instructions_issued: u64,
        l1: Option<L1Counters>,
        l2: Option<L2Counters>,
        dram: Option<DramStats>,
    ) -> KernelReplayResult {
        KernelReplayResult {
            instructions_issued,
            records_seen: instructions_issued,
            per_sm: Default::default(),
            max_cycles: 1,
            l1,
            l2,
            l2_by_source: None,
            dram,
        }
    }

    fn predicted<'a>(preds: &'a [MetricPrediction], key: &str) -> &'a EmitOutcome {
        &preds
            .iter()
            .find(|p| p.key == key)
            .expect("key present")
            .outcome
    }

    /// Emit from owned counters (the `KernelReplayResult` temporary lives
    /// through the `emit_all` call within this expression).
    fn emit(
        instructions_issued: u64,
        l1: Option<L1Counters>,
        l2: Option<L2Counters>,
        dram: Option<DramStats>,
    ) -> Result<Vec<MetricPrediction>, EmitError> {
        emit_all(&CounterSnapshot::from_replay(&replay(
            instructions_issued,
            l1,
            l2,
            dram,
        )))
    }

    #[test]
    fn fraction_is_none_at_zero_denominator_never_zero() {
        let v = MetricValue::fraction("k", 0, 0).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            v,
            MetricValue::Fraction {
                value: None,
                numerator: 0,
                denominator: 0
            }
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn fraction_real_zero_is_some_zero() {
        let MetricValue::Fraction { value, .. } = MetricValue::fraction("k", 0, 10).unwrap() else {
            panic!("expected fraction");
        };
        assert_eq!(value, Some(0.0));
    }

    #[test]
    fn rate_above_unity_is_a_typed_error_not_a_clamp() {
        assert_eq!(
            MetricValue::fraction("k", 11, 10),
            Err(EmitError::RateExceedsUnity {
                key: "k",
                num: 11,
                den: 10
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn op_ld_surface_folds_read_class_bypass_ldgsts_into_the_denominator() {
        // Witness shape: a kernel of ONLY LDGSTS loads (all bypass, none
        // eligible, no atoms) — mirrors gemm_hmma_bf16. The op_ld sector
        // count is the bypass-read stream, and the modeled hit rate is 0
        // (v0 has no L1 residency for bypass) — the honest under-prediction.
        let l1 = L1Counters {
            bypass_sectors: 196_608,
            bypass_atom_sectors: 0,
            store_sectors: 16_384,
            ..Default::default()
        };
        let preds = emit(197_120, Some(l1), None, None).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            predicted(&preds, "traffic_gmem_ld_sectors"),
            &EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::Exact(196_608))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            predicted(&preds, "cache_hit_rate_l1tex_read_sector"),
            &EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::Fraction {
                value: Some(0.0),
                numerator: 0,
                denominator: 196_608
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            predicted(&preds, "traffic_gmem_st_sectors"),
            &EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::Exact(16_384))
        );
        // The instruction count needs no mem unit and is always emitted.
        assert_eq!(
            predicted(&preds, "smsp_inst_executed_sum"),
            &EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::Exact(197_120))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn op_ld_denominator_excludes_the_atom_write_class_bypass_subset() {
        // 100 bypass sectors, 40 of them ATOM (write-class -> op_atom/op_red,
        // NOT op_ld). The op_ld surface sees only the 60 READ-class sectors.
        let l1 = L1Counters {
            hits: 10,
            misses: 5,
            bypass_sectors: 100,
            bypass_atom_sectors: 40,
            ..Default::default()
        };
        let preds = emit(1, Some(l1), None, None).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            predicted(&preds, "traffic_gmem_ld_sectors"),
            &EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::Exact(10 + 5 + 60))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn atom_subset_exceeding_bypass_is_a_typed_counter_invariant() {
        let l1 = L1Counters {
            bypass_sectors: 3,
            bypass_atom_sectors: 4,
            ..Default::default()
        };
        assert_eq!(
            emit(1, Some(l1), None, None),
            Err(EmitError::CounterInvariant {
                key: "traffic_gmem_ld_sectors",
                detail: "bypass_atom_sectors exceeds bypass_sectors (subset invariant broken)",
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn missing_mem_unit_is_unavailable_not_an_error_or_a_zero() {
        // Flat mode: no L1/L2/DRAM. Only the instruction count is produced;
        // every cache metric is typed-unavailable with its needed unit.
        let preds = emit(42, None, None, None).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            predicted(&preds, "smsp_inst_executed_sum"),
            &EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::Exact(42))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            predicted(&preds, "cache_hit_rate_l1tex_read_sector"),
            &EmitOutcome::Unavailable(Unavailable::MemModeLacksUnit {
                needs: MemUnit::L1Tex
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            predicted(&preds, "cache_hit_rate_l2_sector"),
            &EmitOutcome::Unavailable(Unavailable::MemModeLacksUnit {
                needs: MemUnit::Lts
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            predicted(&preds, "traffic_dram_read_sectors"),
            &EmitOutcome::Unavailable(Unavailable::MemModeLacksUnit {
                needs: MemUnit::Dram
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn l2_and_dram_metrics_predict_when_their_units_are_present() {
        let l2 = L2Counters {
            hits: 3,
            misses: 1,
            ..Default::default()
        };
        let dram = DramStats {
            read_sectors: 8415,
            bw_delayed_responses: 0,
        };
        let preds = emit(1, None, Some(l2), Some(dram)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            predicted(&preds, "cache_hit_rate_l2_sector"),
            &EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::Fraction {
                value: Some(0.75),
                numerator: 3,
                denominator: 4
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            predicted(&preds, "traffic_dram_read_sectors"),
            &EmitOutcome::Predicted(MetricValue::Exact(8415))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn index_by_key_covers_every_descriptor() {
        let preds = emit(1, None, None, None).unwrap();
        let idx = index_by_key(&preds);
        assert_eq!(idx.len(), DESCRIPTORS.len());
        for d in DESCRIPTORS {
            assert!(
                idx.contains_key(d.key),
                "descriptor {} missing from index",
                d.key
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn descriptor_keys_are_unique() {
        let mut keys: Vec<&str> = DESCRIPTORS.iter().map(|d| d.key).collect();
        keys.sort_unstable();
        let n = keys.len();
        keys.dedup();
        assert_eq!(keys.len(), n, "duplicate descriptor keys");
    }
}
```

````markdown
# Predictors

> **Current status (2026-07-18).** This page documents retained historical
> predictor lanes. They are external evaluation comparators only and never feed
> simulator features, architecture constants, calibration, or emitted
> predictions. The active product is the Rust event-driven simulator; timing is
> NCU-only, the no-driver-root deployment thesis and dual-source duration path
> are retired, and `gpc__cycles_elapsed.max` is the sole publication-binding
> output. The seven current simulator descriptors are secondary and ungated.

This historical suite was designed to predict GPU kernel performance **without
NCU, without root, and without a GPU-driver profiler surface** at deploy time.
It used three independent **predictor lanes**, each with its own target metric,
model, gate, and — critically — honesty posture per architecture.

The historical results remain only as strong as their recorded gates. sm_86
(RTX 3090 Ti, GA102, Ampere) cache prediction was *validated*; sm_120 (RTX 5060
Laptop, GB206, Blackwell) predictors were *refuted* and are retained as
documented negatives and research hooks; wall-clock was *labels + refutation
only* on both arches. Nothing here launders a refutation into a pass or changes
the active simulator publication contract.

For where these lanes sit in the dataflow, see
[../ARCHITECTURE.md § 3](../ARCHITECTURE.md#3-the-three-predictor-lanes). For the
open sm_120 science, see
[../OPEN_RESEARCH_CHALLENGES.md](../OPEN_RESEARCH_CHALLENGES.md). For why the
merge kept refuted lanes as evidence, see
[../MERGE_PROVENANCE.md § 2](../MERGE_PROVENANCE.md#2-what-was-carried-payload--source--curated-frozen-artifacts).

```
                         THE THREE LANES (target · gate · status)
   ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ Lane A  L2 sector-hit-rate   lts__t_sector_hit_rate.pct   sm_86 VALIDATED   │
   │ Lane B  L1/TEX sector-hit    cache_hit_rate_l1tex_..pct   sm_86 SCORED-only │
   │ Lane C  elapsed cycles       gpc__cycles_elapsed.max      both REFUTED/lbl  │
   └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        every per-arch constant (SM count, geometry, anchor clock, cache-op
        default) is an INPUT card — see arch_profiles/cards/*.json
```

---

## Lane A — L2 sector-hit-rate (parametric prior + v5 monotone head)

**Target metric:** `lts__t_sector_hit_rate.pct`
**Model:** analytical Smith–Eklund stack-distance predictor → learned monotone
calibration head.
**Gate:** `0.06 / 0.15 / 0.25` (median-abs / geomean-rel / holdout-geomean-rel).

### Pipeline

```
 dynamic_trace.pb                                    NCU label (fit-time only)
 (RAW reuse distance,                                lts__t_sector_hit_rate.pct
  recomputed via Fenwick-tree LRU)                          │
        │                                                   │
        ▼                                                   ▼
 ┌──────────────────────┐   raw_pred + 6      ┌──────────────────────────────┐
 │ cache_predictor.py   │   monotone feats    │ v5 PerBucketCalibratorEnsemble│
 │ analytical predictor │────────────────────▶│ IsotonicRegressionOnFrozen    │
 │ modeled-hit rule:    │                     │ Projection  (pygam/LGBM/XGB   │
 │ rd < capacity//32    │                     │  when importable)             │
 │ + gridDim density α  │                     │ monotonic_calibration_head.py │
 │ + L2 high-footprint  │                     └──────────────┬────────────────┘
 │   per-slug factors   │                                    │ calibrated hit rate
 └──────────┬───────────┘                                    ▼
   circular_predictor_input_rejected           ┌──────────────────────────────┐
   (any hrd hit_rate/hit_count input killed)   │  ACCURACY GATE 0.06/0.15/0.25 │
                                               └──────────────┬────────────────┘
              sm_86 ──────► PASS  (Verified-live-sm_86)       │       sm_120
              med-abs 0.0592 <0.06 · geomean 0.0642 <0.15 ────┘       ──► REFUTED
              holdout 0.0552 <0.25 · n=40 admitted (n_fit=34)         (see below)
```

- The analytical stage (`workloads/simbench_bw/cache_predictor.py`) is
  **non-circular by construction**: it recomputes per-launch reuse-distance
  evidence from the producer-side `dynamic_trace.pb`, *not* from the HRD
  profiler's already-modeled `hit_rate`/`hit_count`. Any input carrying those
  fields is rejected with `circular_predictor_input_rejected`
  (`cache_predictor.py:1-21`).
- The head (`monotonic_calibration_head.py`) fits a **per-bucket** ensemble; when
  pygam/LightGBM are unavailable (the pinned env has only sklearn) the only
  fittable class is `IsotonicRegressionOnFrozenProjection` — 1-D PAV on a frozen
  `(raw_prediction, footprint_ratio, long_rd_tail_mass)` projection with weights
  `(+1, −1, −1)` (`monotonic_calibration_head.py:1-39`). Fitter:
  `tools/local_labels/fit_monotonic_calibration_head_v5.py`.

### sm_86 — VALIDATED

Gate thresholds live in
`data/local_labels/calibration_head_v5_accuracy_gates_sm_86.json:143-146`
(`geomean_max 0.15`, `median_abs_max 0.06`, `holdout_max 0.25`, per-bucket p90
0.15 advisory). Frozen head result at HEAD:

| gate | value | bar | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| full-cohort median-abs | **0.05923** | ≤ 0.06 | PASS (barely) |
| full-cohort geomean-rel | **0.06420** | ≤ 0.15 | PASS |
| holdout geomean-rel | **0.05524** | ≤ 0.25 | PASS |
| admitted cells | **40** (n_fit 34, 6 holdout) | — | `Verified-live-sm_86` |

The per-bucket p90 is **advisory** (not admission-blocking): `memory_stress`
0.2346 (n=9) and `other` 0.3587 (n=15) exceed 0.15 but do not fail the gate. The
frozen L2 v5 head is sha-pinned (`sm_86_v5_head.json`,
`d28665f6…`) — see [../MERGE_PROVENANCE.md § 6](../MERGE_PROVENANCE.md#6-byte-identity-proof-the-validated-lane-is-untouched).

### sm_120 — REFUTED (and *why* the frozenset is frozen)

`data/local_labels/sm120_cache_metric_closure.json`:
`verdict = engineering_closure_refuted`, `cache_claim_load_bearing = false`,
`named_target_gate.median_abs_error = 0.27629`, **22** cache/memory targets all
refuted. Root cause is **not** the analytical model — it is the L1→L2 miss
filter going inert on Blackwell:

```
 tools/cache_predictor/l1_cache_op_classifier.py:309
   _BARE_LDG_E_DEFAULTS_TO_CA = frozenset({"sm_86"})          ← sm_120 NOT in set

   sm_86:   bare  LDG.E                → LDG_E_CA   → L1-eligible → filter WORKS
   sm_120:  LDG.E.U16.CONSTANT,             ┐
            desc[UR..] (descriptor loads)   ┴─────► OTHER → bypass → filter INERT
   ⇒ every miss forwarded to L2 unfiltered ⇒ L2 hit-rate prediction refuted
```

Adding `sm_120` to that frozenset **without live evidence is forbidden**: the
promotion trigger requires a live 5060 cuobjdump/microbench to document the true
`.ca`/bypass semantics first. The ArchProfile encodes this fail-closed — the
sm_120 card carries `"bare_ldg_e_default": "unknown_typed_unavailable"`
(`arch_profiles/cards/sm_120-laptop.json`), so bare `LDG.E` keeps mapping to
`OTHER`. The `cache_replay` subsystem (`data/local_labels/cache_replay_*.json`)
is a **non-load-bearing sm_120 ablation**, not a predictor: even its best learned
arm scores 0.0755 median-abs — still above the 0.055 target — so it cannot rescue
the lane. Full detail:
[../OPEN_RESEARCH_CHALLENGES.md § 1](../OPEN_RESEARCH_CHALLENGES.md#challenge-1--sm_120-blackwell-l2-cache-hit-prediction-is-unsolved).

---

## Lane B — L1/TEX sector-hit-rate (walker + classifier + bounded head)

**Target metric:** `cache_hit_rate_l1tex_sector_pct`
**Model:** per-SM LRU walker → cache-op classifier → bounded-[0,1] calibration head.
**Gate:** coverage-gated, **NOT accuracy-gated** (this is the honesty crux).

### Pipeline

```
 cuobjdump SASS text ─► l1_cache_op_classifier.py ─► per-PC cache-op map
                        (12-token wire vocab:          (which accesses are
                         LDG_E_CA … OTHER,              L1-eligible vs bypass)
                         host-only, no NVBit)                    │
                                                                 ▼
 per-block access seq ─► l1_walker.py ──────────────► per-launch L1 hit counters
 (line_id, l1_eligible)   per-SM fully-assoc LRU,      (bypass excluded from BOTH
                          sector-with-line-alloc hit    numerator & denominator)
                          cap = capacity_bytes // 128           │
                                                                ▼
                                              bounded-[0,1] L1 head → COVERAGE gate
                                              (sm_86_l1_head.json)         │
                          sm_86 ──► SCORED (meets_floor=true) ─────────────┘
                          rel-geomean 0.89 · n=44 (30 scalar / 14 typed_unavail)
                          NO hard accuracy gate · median abs residual ≈ 4%
                          sm_120 ──► UNCALIBRATED (no L1 head; cache_layers=["L2"])
```

- The walker (`tools/cache_predictor/l1_walker.py`) models each SM's L1 as an
  independent fully-associative LRU line cache (CTAs on different SMs do not evict
  each other). Hit rule = **sector-with-line-allocation**; bypass accesses
  (`l1_eligible=False`) are excluded from both numerator and denominator.
- The classifier (`l1_cache_op_classifier.py`) records the **actual SASS opcode**,
  not the semantic class: the Blackwell `.ca` encoding `LDG.E.STRONG.SM` is kept
  as `LDG_E_STRONG_SM` (L1-bypass on Blackwell), never collapsed into the Ampere
  `LDG_E_CA`. It is cuobjdump-backed and host-only.

### sm_86 — SCORED, not accuracy-gated

`data/local_labels/l1_closure_comparison_sm_86.json`: `result_kind = admitted`,
`relative_error_stats_l1tex.geomean = 0.8905` over **44** cells (30 scalar / 14
`typed_unavailable`), `coverage_gate_verdict.meets_floor = true`. The apparent
"0.89 error" is a **relative-geomean artifact**: L1 hit rates on streaming kernels
sit near zero, so `|pred−true|/true` inflates even though the **median absolute
residual is ≈ 4%** (q50 ≈ 0.041). There is deliberately **no hard L1 accuracy
gate** in the runner — "L1 load-bearing" means *scored + coverage-gated*, held to
the L2 standard only for coverage, never for accuracy. `cache_layers` is a
per-arch card: `sm_86 → ["L1","L2"]`.

### sm_120 — UNCALIBRATED

No sm_120 L1 head, no sm_120 L1 predictions exist; the sm_120 card forces
`cache_layers = ["L2"]` so no L1TEX cell is broadcast (a uniform `["L1","L2"]`
would flood every sm_120 L1 cell as `join_key_unmatched`). The two Blackwell-only
classifier tokens are exercised via canned cuobjdump text fixtures only; live
sm_120 coverage defers to a cross-arch follow-up. See
[../OPEN_RESEARCH_CHALLENGES.md § 3](../OPEN_RESEARCH_CHALLENGES.md#challenge-3--sm_120-l1tex-prediction-is-uncalibrated).

---

## Lane C — wall-clock (historical comparator; nonbinding)

**Historical target metric:** `gpc__cycles_elapsed.max` — an elapsed cycle
count that avoids direct nanosecond-to-frequency conversion but is **not assumed
DVFS-stable**. It is the sole publication-binding target in the current
simulator contract. Nanoseconds were a derived interval in this retired predictor lane, never a
co-equal point.
**Model:** roofline prior + ridge residual (`pedestal_roofline_ridge_residual`).
**Merge policy:** **labels + refutation only** — no positive wall-clock claim ships.
The thresholds and diagram below preserve the retired predictor's own gate; they
are not the ADR-0002 MAPE evaluator or M-SIM-1.

### Why cycles, not nanoseconds

Predicting `duration_ns` directly inherits the DVFS confound. Tree B's
OLS-on-`log10(duration_ns)` is **refuted** in
`data/local_labels/duration_predictor_report.json`: held-out SMAPE **1.766** vs
the strongest baseline (`shape_size_only`) **0.891** — and the NVML clock
covariates are the *entire harmful delta* (`predictor_smape_without_nvml` equals
the baseline exactly). The clock spanned **180–2762 MHz (15.34×)** across the
cohort. The historical cycles formulation avoided making the observed
nanosecond-to-clock conversion itself the prediction target; it did not prove
frequency invariance. Every retained observation remains bound to its recorded
operating state.

### Pipeline

```
 launch geometry + static SASS work + GA102 peak constants
        │
        ▼
 ┌─────────────────────────────┐   FORBIDDEN_FEATURE_FIELDS blocks labels as
 │ timing_cycle_predictor.py   │   inputs: gpc__cycles_elapsed.max, gpu__time_
 │ roofline prior:             │   duration.sum, clock64, IPC, occupancy …
 │   dyn-FLOP ÷ tensor peak     │   (deploy-legal feature vector only)
 │   × 0.066 efficiency prior   │
 │ + ridge residual (λ=10)      │──────────────┐  predicted cycles
 │ v3 same-slug arm → DIAGNOSTIC│              │
 └─────────────────────────────┘              ▼
                              ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
                              │ HISTORICAL GATE (nonbinding):             │
   sm_86 CYCLE HEADLINE ─────▶│  geomean-rel ≤0.15 · med-abs-log ≤0.1     │
   med-abs-log 0.0414  PASS   │  bootstrap-upper ≤0.25 · ≥10 cells        │
   geomean-rel 0.1583  FAIL ──┤                                           │
   bootstrap    0.3099 FAIL ──┘  ⇒ verdict_falsification (n=13, GEMM-heavy)│
                              └──────────────────────────────────────────┘
        │ cycles × 1000 / mhz × [1 ± 0.06]      (mhz = short-burst 1890 anchor)
        ▼
 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ DEPLOY-ns CROSSWALK (separate leg): CUPTI-Activity & cudaEvent vs NCU  │
 │  agreement_pass on 13/13 cells · noise floor 110352 ns · bound 0.20    │
 │  ⇒ research_success  (ns is a DERIVED interval, not a point headline)  │
 └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

- The predictor (`timing_cycle_predictor.py`) is deploy-legal: labels can be fit
  targets but never inference inputs (`FORBIDDEN_FEATURE_FIELDS`, line 100). The
  v3 same-slug scaled-neighbor arm was **demoted to a diagnostic-only channel**;
  the deployable score uses no same-slug substitution.
- The short-burst **1890 MHz** anchor (not the 1350 MHz sustained-throttle anchor)
  removes the ~38% cycles→ns bias; the ns leg emits an interval via
  `cycles_to_ns(..., regime="short_burst") × [1 ± 0.06]` (`timing_closure.py:79`).

### Status

`data/local_labels/timing_predictions/timing_closure_sm_86.json`:
`cycle_terminal_state = verdict_falsification` (an **honest near-miss** — geomean
is 0.008 over the bar; the n=13 GEMM-heavy cohort's bootstrap upper bound is
clearly over), `deploy_ns_terminal_state = research_success`,
`overall_terminal_state = verdict_falsification`. The historical predictor cycle
gate therefore **did not pass**; only its now-retired deploy-ns crosswalk
closed. This result has no authority over ADR-0002 or M-SIM-1.
**sm_120** has no cycle labels and no short-burst anchor →
`deferred_requires_sm120_cycle_capture`; the refuted OLS is not carried forward. See
[../OPEN_RESEARCH_CHALLENGES.md § 4](../OPEN_RESEARCH_CHALLENGES.md#challenge-4--wall-clock--duration-prediction-is-unsolved-on-both-arches).

---

## Cross-lane invariants

| property | Lane A (L2) | Lane B (L1) | Lane C (cycles) |
|---|---|---|---|
| sm_86 status | **VALIDATED** (gate pass) | **SCORED** (coverage only) | cycle near-miss / **ns pass** |
| sm_120 status | **REFUTED** | uncalibrated | **deferred** |
| hard accuracy gate | 0.06 / 0.15 / 0.25 | none (by design) | 0.15 / 0.10 / 0.25 |
| deploy-legal features | yes | yes | yes (`FORBIDDEN_FEATURE_FIELDS`) |
| per-arch knobs | ArchProfile card | ArchProfile card | ArchProfile card |

Every per-arch number a lane touches — SM count, L1/L2 geometry, `griddim_penalty_alpha`,
`bare_ldg_e_default`, the NVML anchor clocks, `cache_layers` — is an **input card**
under `arch_profiles/cards/`, resolved by `arch_profiles/loader.py` with
**fail-closed** behavior on unknown devices (no silent sm_86 fallback). That
decoupling is the whole point of the merge:
[../ARCHITECTURE.md § 4](../ARCHITECTURE.md#4-the-archprofile-system).

The SOL-ExecBench baseline corpus that feeds kernels into these lanes is
documented at [sol_execbench/README.md](sol_execbench/README.md).
````

```rust
//! Trace → SM replay driver: flattens one traced kernel launch into per-SM
//! block replays using the REAL hardware placement recorded in the trace
//! (per-instruction `sm_id` / `warpid_sm`), joins each dynamic record to
//! the issue schedule (and, when an L1 setup is supplied, to the cache-op
//! manifest + per-record unique-sector expansion), and runs the issue
//! model on every SM.
//!
//! Placement policy v0: the traced placement IS the model — each block
//! runs on the SM the hardware ran it on, each warp on its physical warp
//! slot. Traces without `sm_id` are a typed error (a synthetic placement
//! model is a future knob, not a silent fallback).
//!
//! Memory-record classification (L1 mode): a global-class record takes
//! the [`MemRole`] its pc's SIDECAR OPCODE was classified to at join
//! time (`sim_mem::cache_op` port of the Python token rules) — eligible
//! load → modeled L1 sectors; bypass load → counted bypass; store head →
//! hit-tested without allocating; everything else → unified-denominator
//! count only. Sector expansion follows the `l1_trace_adapter` contract:
//! per-lane `addr>>5 ..= (addr+width-1)>>5`, deduplicated per INSTRUCTION
//! in first-seen order (active lanes are the non-sentinel slots — the
//! canonical positional guarantee).
//!
//! v0 limitation (fail-closed, not silent): every dynamic record of a
//! launch must carry the launch's own `function_unique_id` — traced device
//! function CALLs would need per-segment schedules and are rejected typed
//! until a trace exercises them (none of the 17 M1 traces does).
//!
//! Memory discipline: blocks are decoded ONE at a time and compacted
//! immediately (12-byte records + a per-warp sector arena); the prost tree
//! is dropped before the next block loads.

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
use std::path::PathBuf;

use sim_mem::{L1Config, L1Counters, push_unique_sectors};
use sim_trace::lanes::LANE_INACTIVE_SENTINEL;
use sim_trace::pb;
use sim_trace::{
    KernelLoc, TraceDir, TraceError, block_launch_index, check_allocation_identity, kernel_grid,
    read_threadblock, visit_memory_access,
};

use sim_mem::{L2Config, L2Counters, L2Model, MemRole};

use crate::issue::{
    AccessKind, BlockReplay, IssueError, IssueModelParams, ReplayInst, SmSimResult, WarpReplay,
    simulate_sm,
};
use crate::program::FunctionSchedule;
use crate::system::{DramBw, DramStats, L2SourceSplit, SystemError, simulate_kernel_shared};

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum ReplayError {
    #[error(transparent)]
    Trace(#[from] TraceError),
    #[error(transparent)]
    Issue(#[from] IssueError),
    #[error(transparent)]
    System(#[from] SystemError),
    #[error("L2 config invalid: {0}")]
    L2Config(#[from] sim_mem::L2ConfigError),
    #[error("no issue schedule for function_unique_id {function_unique_id}")]
    ScheduleMissing { function_unique_id: i32 },
    #[error(
        "{path}: warp {warp_id} record {record_ix} carries function_unique_id {found}, launch \
         kernel is {expected} — multi-function replay is not supported in v0"
    )]
    MultiFunctionUnsupported {
        path: PathBuf,
        warp_id: i32,
        record_ix: usize,
        expected: i32,
        found: i32,
    },
    #[error("{path}: no instruction record carries sm_id — v0 replay requires traced placement")]
    SmIdMissing { path: PathBuf },
    #[error(
        "{path}: sm_id changes within the block ({first} then {second}) — blocks never migrate"
    )]
    SmIdInconsistent {
        path: PathBuf,
        first: i32,
        second: i32,
    },
    #[error("{path}: warp {warp_id} warpid_sm changes within the warp ({first} then {second})")]
    WarpSlotInconsistent {
        path: PathBuf,
        warp_id: i32,
        first: i32,
        second: i32,
    },
    #[error(
        "{path}: warp {warp_id} has no warpid_sm on any record — v0 replay requires the traced \
         physical warp slot (sub-core assignment), like sm_id"
    )]
    WarpSlotMissing { path: PathBuf, warp_id: i32 },
    #[error(
        "{path}: warp {warp_id} record {record_ix}: {sectors} unique sectors in one record \
         overflows the u16 arena index"
    )]
    SectorCountOverflow {
        path: PathBuf,
        warp_id: i32,
        record_ix: usize,
        sectors: usize,
    },
    #[error("duplicate block launch index {index} across threadblock files")]
    DuplicateLaunchIndex { index: i64 },
    #[error(
        "issued {issued} != records {records} — replay invariant broken (every traced record \
         must issue exactly once)"
    )]
    CountMismatch { issued: u64, records: u64 },
    #[error(
        "E_INCOMPLETE_TRACE: {seen}/{grid_total} launch blocks present and no \
         trace_sampling.json sidecar — an incomplete trace must carry a sampling sidecar"
    )]
    IncompleteTrace { seen: u64, grid_total: u64 },
    #[error(
        "trace_sampling sidecar original_grid {sidecar:?} != launch gridDim {launch:?} \
         (a subset must NEVER rewrite gridDim)"
    )]
    GridDimRewritten {
        launch: (u32, u32, u32),
        sidecar: (u32, u32, u32),
    },
    #[error("records_seen {records_seen} != trace_sampling sidecar records.captured {captured}")]
    RecordsCapturedMismatch { records_seen: u64, captured: u64 },
    #[error(
        "trace_sampling sidecar selected block membership does not match replayed threadblocks \
         ({seen} seen, {declared} declared)"
    )]
    SelectedBlockMembershipMismatch { seen: u64, declared: u64 },
    #[error("trace_sampling sidecar kernel {sidecar:?} != launch kernel {launch:?}")]
    SamplingKernelMismatch { launch: String, sidecar: String },
    #[error("kernel launch block_dim is absent or degenerate")]
    BlockDimMissing,
    #[error("trace_sampling sidecar original_block {sidecar:?} != launch blockDim {launch:?}")]
    BlockDimRewritten {
        launch: (u32, u32, u32),
        sidecar: (u32, u32, u32),
    },
}

/// Replay outcome for one kernel launch.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct KernelReplayResult {
    /// Exact by construction: one issue per traced record (invariant-checked
    /// against `records_seen`).
    pub instructions_issued: u64,
    pub records_seen: u64,
    /// Per traced SM id.
    pub per_sm: BTreeMap<i32, SmSimResult>,
    /// Directional v0 proxy for `gpc__cycles_elapsed.max`.
    pub max_cycles: u64,
    /// Kernel-level L1 counters (sum over per-SM caches) in L1 mode.
    pub l1: Option<L1Counters>,
    /// Shared-L2 counters (the `replay_kernel_shared` path only).
    pub l2: Option<L2Counters>,
    /// Per-source L2 split from the driver-side emission observer.
    pub l2_by_source: Option<L2SourceSplit>,
    /// DRAM read-traffic observer (shared mode only).
    pub dram: Option<DramStats>,
}

/// Decode one launch into per-SM block replays on the traced placement.
/// `decode_sectors` selects the L1-mode classification (lane decode +
/// unique-sector expansion) over the flat-mode class check.
fn extract_per_sm_blocks(
    td: &TraceDir,
    loc: &KernelLoc<'_>,
    schedule: &FunctionSchedule,
    decode_sectors: bool,
) -> Result<(BTreeMap<i32, Vec<BlockReplay>>, u64), ReplayError> {
    let expected_fuid = schedule.function_unique_id;
    // sm_id → blocks (launch index kept for in-SM ordering).
    let mut per_sm_blocks: BTreeMap<i32, Vec<BlockReplay>> = BTreeMap::new();
    let mut seen_indices: BTreeSet<i64> = BTreeSet::new();
    let mut records_seen: u64 = 0;

    for path in td.threadblock_paths(loc)? {
        let tb = read_threadblock(&path)?;
        let launch_index = block_launch_index(loc.kernel, &tb, &path)?;
        if !seen_indices.insert(launch_index) {
            return Err(ReplayError::DuplicateLaunchIndex {
                index: launch_index,
            });
        }

        let mut block_sm: Option<i32> = None;
        let mut warps = Vec::with_capacity(tb.warps.len());
        for (&warp_id, warp) in &tb.warps {
            let mut warp_slot: Option<i32> = None;
            let mut insts = Vec::with_capacity(warp.instructions.len());
            let mut sectors: Vec<i64> = Vec::new();
            for (record_ix, inst) in warp.instructions.iter().enumerate() {
                records_seen += 1;
                // Allocation-identity gate on the path the simulator actually
                // consumes: a GLOBAL/GENERIC-space active record (ordinary global,
                // global atomic, LDGSTS source) must carry a resolvable, in-range
                // allocation id — parity with the Python validator and the
                // TraceDir reader. Fail-closed BEFORE classification so a
                // malformed record never reaches the L1/L2 model.
                check_allocation_identity(inst, td.allocations(), || {
                    format!("{} warp={warp_id} inst={record_ix}", path.display())
                })?;
                if inst.function_unique_id != expected_fuid {
                    return Err(ReplayError::MultiFunctionUnsupported {
                        path,
                        warp_id,
                        record_ix,
                        expected: expected_fuid,
                        found: inst.function_unique_id,
                    });
                }
                if let Some(sm) = inst.sm_id {
                    match block_sm {
                        None => block_sm = Some(sm),
                        Some(first) if first != sm => {
                            return Err(ReplayError::SmIdInconsistent {
                                path,
                                first,
                                second: sm,
                            });
                        }
                        Some(_) => {}
                    }
                }
                if let Some(slot) = inst.warpid_sm {
                    match warp_slot {
                        None => warp_slot = Some(slot),
                        Some(first) if first != slot => {
                            return Err(ReplayError::WarpSlotInconsistent {
                                path,
                                warp_id,
                                first,
                                second: slot,
                            });
                        }
                        Some(_) => {}
                    }
                }
                let kind = if decode_sectors {
                    classify_with_l1(inst, schedule, &mut sectors, &path, warp_id, record_ix)?
                } else {
                    classify_flat(inst, &path, warp_id, record_ix)?
                };
                insts.push(ReplayInst { pc: inst.pc, kind });
            }
            // Fail-closed traced placement: a warp that issued records
            // without ever exposing its physical slot is a typed error,
            // exactly like a block without sm_id (a synthetic placement
            // model is a future knob, never a silent fallback). Warps
            // with NO records carry no placement and issue nothing.
            let warp_slot = match warp_slot {
                Some(slot) => slot,
                None if insts.is_empty() => warp_id,
                None => {
                    return Err(ReplayError::WarpSlotMissing { path, warp_id });
                }
            };
            warps.push(WarpReplay {
                warp_slot,
                insts,
                sectors,
            });
        }
        let Some(sm) = block_sm else {
            return Err(ReplayError::SmIdMissing { path });
        };
        per_sm_blocks.entry(sm).or_default().push(BlockReplay {
            launch_index,
            warps,
        });
    }
    // Completeness gate (fail-closed) on the path replay ACTUALLY consumes: a
    // subset trace (coverage < grid) is admissible ONLY with a valid
    // trace_sampling.json sidecar whose original_grid matches the launch record
    // (gridDim is never rewritten) and whose captured record count matches
    // records_seen. Absent/non-sampling sidecars never waive full coverage.
    let (gx, gy, gz) = kernel_grid(loc.kernel)?;
    let grid_total = u64::from(gx) * u64::from(gy) * u64::from(gz);
    let seen = seen_indices.len() as u64;
    match td.sampling_sidecar() {
        None => {
            if seen < grid_total {
                return Err(ReplayError::IncompleteTrace { seen, grid_total });
            }
        }
        Some(sc) => {
            let block = loc
                .kernel
                .block_dim
                .as_ref()
                .filter(|dim| dim.x > 0 && dim.y > 0 && dim.z > 0)
                .ok_or(ReplayError::BlockDimMissing)?;
            let launch_block = (block.x as u32, block.y as u32, block.z as u32);
            if sc.kernel_mangled_name != loc.kernel.name {
                return Err(ReplayError::SamplingKernelMismatch {
                    launch: loc.kernel.name.clone(),
                    sidecar: sc.kernel_mangled_name.clone(),
                });
            }
            if sc.original_grid != (gx, gy, gz) {
                return Err(ReplayError::GridDimRewritten {
                    launch: (gx, gy, gz),
                    sidecar: sc.original_grid,
                });
            }
            if sc.original_block != launch_block {
                return Err(ReplayError::BlockDimRewritten {
                    launch: launch_block,
                    sidecar: sc.original_block,
                });
            }
            if sc.sanctions_incomplete && sc.selected_block_ids.as_ref() != Some(&seen_indices) {
                return Err(ReplayError::SelectedBlockMembershipMismatch {
                    seen,
                    declared: sc
                        .selected_block_ids
                        .as_ref()
                        .map_or(0, |blocks| blocks.len() as u64),
                });
            }
            if seen < grid_total && !sc.sanctions_incomplete {
                return Err(ReplayError::IncompleteTrace { seen, grid_total });
            }
            if records_seen != sc.captured_records {
                return Err(ReplayError::RecordsCapturedMismatch {
                    records_seen,
                    captured: sc.captured_records,
                });
            }
        }
    }
    for blocks in per_sm_blocks.values_mut() {
        blocks.sort_by_key(|b| b.launch_index);
    }
    Ok((per_sm_blocks, records_seen))
}

/// Fold per-SM results into the kernel-level view, enforcing the
/// one-issue-per-record invariant.
fn fold_kernel_result(
    per_sm: BTreeMap<i32, SmSimResult>,
    records_seen: u64,
    l2: Option<(L2Counters, L2SourceSplit, DramStats)>,
) -> Result<KernelReplayResult, ReplayError> {
    let mut instructions_issued: u64 = 0;
    let mut max_cycles: u64 = 0;
    let mut l1_totals: Option<L1Counters> = None;
    for result in per_sm.values() {
        instructions_issued += result.instructions_issued;
        max_cycles = max_cycles.max(result.cycles);
        if let Some(c) = &result.l1 {
            l1_totals.get_or_insert_with(L1Counters::default).add(c);
        }
    }
    if instructions_issued != records_seen {
        return Err(ReplayError::CountMismatch {
            issued: instructions_issued,
            records: records_seen,
        });
    }
    let (l2, l2_by_source, dram) = match l2 {
        Some((counters, split, dram)) => (Some(counters), Some(split), Some(dram)),
        None => (None, None, None),
    };
    Ok(KernelReplayResult {
        instructions_issued,
        records_seen,
        per_sm,
        max_cycles,
        l1: l1_totals,
        l2,
        l2_by_source,
        dram,
    })
}

fn lookup_schedule<'a>(
    schedules: &'a BTreeMap<i32, FunctionSchedule>,
    loc: &KernelLoc<'_>,
) -> Result<&'a FunctionSchedule, ReplayError> {
    let expected_fuid = loc.kernel.function_unique_id;
    schedules
        .get(&expected_fuid)
        .ok_or(ReplayError::ScheduleMissing {
            function_unique_id: expected_fuid,
        })
}

/// Memory-hierarchy mode for one kernel replay — the ONE typed selector
/// every harness goes through (a pair of optional configs would let a
/// plumbing slip degrade a cell to the wrong mode silently).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub enum ReplayMemMode {
    /// No cache model (flat global latency).
    Flat,
    /// Per-SM L1s with constant fill latency below them (the pre-L2
    /// lockstep/ablation surface).
    L1Const(L1Config),
    /// Per-SM L1s over ONE shared L2 (the full hierarchy): L1 misses
    /// priced L2-hit vs DRAM by the shared state through the event
    /// system.
    L1SharedL2 {
        l1: L1Config,
        l2: L2Config,
        dram: DramBw,
    },
}

/// Replay one kernel launch on its traced placement under `mode`.
/// Caches are FRESH per kernel (cold, NCU `--cache-control all` parity).
pub fn replay_kernel(
    td: &TraceDir,
    loc: &KernelLoc<'_>,
    schedules: &BTreeMap<i32, FunctionSchedule>,
    params: &IssueModelParams,
    mode: ReplayMemMode,
) -> Result<KernelReplayResult, ReplayError> {
    let schedule = lookup_schedule(schedules, loc)?;
    let decode_sectors = !matches!(mode, ReplayMemMode::Flat);
    let (per_sm_blocks, records_seen) = extract_per_sm_blocks(td, loc, schedule, decode_sectors)?;
    match mode {
        ReplayMemMode::Flat | ReplayMemMode::L1Const(_) => {
            let l1_config = match mode {
                ReplayMemMode::L1Const(cfg) => Some(cfg),
                _ => None,
            };
            let mut per_sm = BTreeMap::new();
            for (sm, blocks) in &per_sm_blocks {
                per_sm.insert(*sm, simulate_sm(blocks, schedule, params, l1_config)?);
            }
            fold_kernel_result(per_sm, records_seen, None)
        }
        ReplayMemMode::L1SharedL2 { l1, l2, dram } => {
            let mut l2 = L2Model::new(l2)?;
            let sys = simulate_kernel_shared(&per_sm_blocks, schedule, params, l1, &mut l2, dram)?;
            fold_kernel_result(
                sys.per_sm,
                records_seen,
                Some((sys.l2, sys.l2_by_source, sys.dram)),
            )
        }
    }
}

/// Fast-path classification when no L1 model is attached: memory class
/// only, no lane decode — but the SAME wire-contract violations the L1
/// path rejects via `visit_memory_access` are rejected here with the
/// SAME typed diagnoses (a malformed record must never pass one mode
/// and fail the other).
///
/// Note: flat mode reuses `GlobalUntagged { off: 0, len: 0 }` as its
/// "global-class, sectors not decoded" encoding; `AccessKind` consumers
/// must not read flat-mode replays as untagged-pc statistics (no L1
/// counters exist in this mode).
fn classify_flat(
    inst: &pb::Instruction,
    path: &std::path::Path,
    warp_id: i32,
    record_ix: usize,
) -> Result<AccessKind, ReplayError> {
    let record = || format!("{} warp={warp_id} inst={record_ix}", path.display());
    let Some(raw) = inst.memory_op_class else {
        // Memory-ness contract: address payloads without a memory class
        // are a typed violation (mirrors the reader).
        if inst.addresses.is_empty() {
            return Ok(AccessKind::NonMemory);
        }
        return Err(TraceError::MemoryOpClassMissing {
            record: record(),
            n_addresses: inst.addresses.len(),
        }
        .into());
    };
    match pb::MemoryOpClass::try_from(raw) {
        Ok(pb::MemoryOpClass::Shared) => Ok(AccessKind::Shared),
        Ok(pb::MemoryOpClass::Unspecified) => {
            // Contract violation, NOT schema skew — same diagnosis as
            // the reader path.
            Err(TraceError::MemoryOpClassUnspecified { record: record() }.into())
        }
        Err(_) => Err(TraceError::UnknownEnumValue {
            record: record(),
            field: "memory_op_class",
            raw,
        }
        .into()),
        Ok(_) => {
            // Route a shared-space record (a shared atomic ATOMS carries
            // op_class=ATOMIC but address_space=SHARED) out of the global path,
            // even in flat mode where sectors are not decoded. Per-address
            // space is authoritative; absent falls back to global.
            let shared_space = inst.addresses.iter().any(|a| {
                matches!(
                    a.address_space
                        .and_then(|r| pb::MemorySpace::try_from(r).ok()),
                    Some(pb::MemorySpace::Shared) | Some(pb::MemorySpace::Local)
                )
            });
            if shared_space {
                Ok(AccessKind::Shared)
            } else {
                Ok(AccessKind::GlobalUntagged { off: 0, len: 0 })
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Full classification in L1 mode: wire-contract decode (streaming form),
/// per-instruction unique-sector expansion into the warp arena, and the
/// join-time [`MemRole`] split.
fn classify_with_l1(
    inst: &pb::Instruction,
    schedule: &FunctionSchedule,
    sectors: &mut Vec<i64>,
    path: &std::path::Path,
    warp_id: i32,
    record_ix: usize,
) -> Result<AccessKind, ReplayError> {
    let start = sectors.len();
    let record = || format!("{} warp={warp_id} inst={record_ix}", path.display());
    let mut effective_space: Option<pb::MemorySpace> = None;
    let meta = visit_memory_access(inst, record, |a| {
        if effective_space.is_none() {
            effective_space = a.address_space;
        }
        push_unique_sectors(
            &a.lane_vector,
            (0..a.lane_vector.len()).filter(|&i| a.lane_vector[i] != LANE_INACTIVE_SENTINEL),
            a.data_width_bytes,
            sectors,
            start,
        );
    })?;
    let Some(meta) = meta else {
        return Ok(AccessKind::NonMemory);
    };
    // Route by EFFECTIVE per-address space, not the instruction-level op_class:
    // a shared atomic (ATOMS) carries op_class=ATOMIC but address_space=SHARED,
    // and must not enter the global L1TEX/L2 sector stream. The per-address
    // space is authoritative when present; absent (legacy traces) falls back to
    // the instruction-level Shared class.
    let shared_space = matches!(
        effective_space,
        Some(pb::MemorySpace::Shared) | Some(pb::MemorySpace::Local)
    );
    if meta.op_class == pb::MemoryOpClass::Shared || shared_space {
        // Shared-window addresses never enter the L1TEX sector stream.
        sectors.truncate(start);
        return Ok(AccessKind::Shared);
    }
    let count = sectors.len() - start;
    let overflow = |sectors: usize| ReplayError::SectorCountOverflow {
        path: path.to_path_buf(),
        warp_id,
        record_ix,
        sectors,
    };
    let off = u32::try_from(start).map_err(|_| overflow(start))?;
    let len = u16::try_from(count).map_err(|_| overflow(count))?;
    // A pc absent from the schedule surfaces as the issue loop's typed
    // PcNotInSchedule; classify neutrally here.
    let role = schedule
        .by_pc
        .get(&u64::from(inst.pc))
        .map_or(MemRole::None, |slot| slot.mem_role);
    Ok(match role {
        MemRole::EligibleLoad(token) => AccessKind::GlobalEligible { off, len, token },
        MemRole::BypassLoad(token) => AccessKind::GlobalBypass { off, len, token },
        MemRole::Store => AccessKind::GlobalStore { off, len },
        MemRole::None => AccessKind::GlobalUntagged { off, len },
    })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod space_routing_tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::path::Path;

    /// An ATOMIC-class instruction carrying a single address record whose
    /// per-address space is `space` (None = legacy, no address_space).
    fn atomic_inst(space: Option<pb::MemorySpace>) -> pb::Instruction {
        let mut a = pb::Address::default();
        a.addrs = vec![0x1000];
        a.address_space = space.map(|s| s as i32);
        pb::Instruction {
            memory_op_class: Some(pb::MemoryOpClass::Atomic as i32),
            addresses: vec![a],
            ..Default::default()
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn flat_shared_atomic_routes_to_shared_not_global() {
        // The blocking corruption: a shared atomic (op_class=ATOMIC,
        // address_space=SHARED) must NOT reach the global path.
        let k = classify_flat(
            &atomic_inst(Some(pb::MemorySpace::Shared)),
            Path::new("t"),
            0,
            0,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(k, AccessKind::Shared));
    }

    #[test]
    fn flat_global_atomic_routes_to_global() {
        let k = classify_flat(
            &atomic_inst(Some(pb::MemorySpace::Global)),
            Path::new("t"),
            0,
            0,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(k, AccessKind::GlobalUntagged { .. }));
    }

    #[test]
    fn flat_legacy_atomic_without_space_falls_back_to_global() {
        let k = classify_flat(&atomic_inst(None), Path::new("t"), 0, 0).unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(k, AccessKind::GlobalUntagged { .. }));
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod replay_identity_tests {
    //! The allocation-identity gate is enforced on the path the simulator
    //! actually consumes (extract_per_sm_blocks), not only in a helper: a
    //! malformed GLOBAL-space global-atomic or LDGSTS-source record fails closed
    //! BEFORE replay classification.
    use super::*;
    use crate::program::FunctionSchedule;
    use prost::Message;
    use std::collections::BTreeMap as StdMap;

    /// A GLOBAL-space memory instruction of `op_class` with NO allocation_id —
    /// malformed under the address-carrying contract's identity rule.
    fn malformed_global_inst(op_class: pb::MemoryOpClass) -> pb::Instruction {
        let mut addrs = vec![0x7000_0000i64];
        addrs.extend(std::iter::repeat(LANE_INACTIVE_SENTINEL).take(31));
        pb::Instruction {
            pc: 16,
            active_mask: Some(0b1),
            predicate_mask: Some(0b1),
            function_unique_id: 1,
            vpc: Some(16),
            sm_id: Some(0),
            warpid_sm: Some(0),
            warpid_tb: Some(0),
            data_width: Some(4),
            memory_op_class: Some(op_class as i32),
            memory_op_access_kind: Some(pb::MemoryOpAccessKind::Atomic as i32),
            addresses: vec![pb::Address {
                data_width: 4,
                compression_format: 0, // list_all
                addrs,
                allocation_id: None, // malformed: GLOBAL active record, no id
                address_space: Some(pb::MemorySpace::Global as i32),
                ..Default::default()
            }],
            ..Default::default()
        }
    }

    fn write_trace_with(dir: &std::path::Path, inst: pb::Instruction) {
        let kernel = pb::Kernel {
            id: 1,
            name: "k".into(),
            function_unique_id: 1,
            size_shared_memory: 0,
            number_of_registers: 32,
            shared_memory_base_address: 0,
            local_memory_base_address: 0,
            grid_dim: Some(pb::Dim3d { x: 1, y: 1, z: 1 }),
            block_dim: Some(pb::Dim3d { x: 32, y: 1, z: 1 }),
            cluster_dim: Some(pb::Dim3d { x: 1, y: 1, z: 1 }),
        };
        let stream = pb::CudaStream {
            id: 0,
            kernels: vec![kernel],
            ordered_cuda_events: vec![],
        };
        let device = pb::GpuDevice {
            id: 0,
            streams: [(0i64, stream)].into_iter().collect(),
        };
        let trace = pb::Trace {
            name: "m".into(),
            binary_version: 1,
            nvbit_version: "1.8".into(),
            accelsim_version: 0,
            is_gathered_registers_values: false,
            gpu_device: [(0i64, device)].into_iter().collect(),
            trace_contract_id: String::new(),
            memory_payload_classes: vec![],
        };
        std::fs::write(dir.join("dynamic_trace.pb"), trace.encode_to_vec()).unwrap();
        // A VALID sidecar, so a missing id is AllocationIdMissing (not
        // AllocationsSidecarMissing) — the record itself is what is malformed.
        let extra = dir.join("extra_info");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&extra).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(
            extra.join("allocations.json"),
            r#"[{"allocation_id":1,"context_id":1,"device_id":0,"base_address":"0x70000000","size_bytes":4096,"alive":true}]"#,
        )
        .unwrap();
        let tb_dir = dir.join("threadblocks/device_0/stream_0/kernel_1");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&tb_dir).unwrap();
        let warp = pb::Warp {
            id: 0,
            instructions: vec![inst],
        };
        let tb = pb::Threadblock {
            block_id: Some(pb::Dim3d { x: 0, y: 0, z: 0 }),
            warps: [(0i32, warp)].into_iter().collect(),
        };
        std::fs::write(tb_dir.join("d_0_s_0_k_1_0,0,0.pb"), tb.encode_to_vec()).unwrap();
    }

    fn assert_replay_rejects_identity(inst: pb::Instruction) {
        let tmp = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        write_trace_with(tmp.path(), inst);
        let td = TraceDir::open(tmp.path()).unwrap();
        let loc = td.kernels().next().unwrap();
        let sched = FunctionSchedule {
            function_unique_id: 1,
            kernel_name: "k".into(),
            function_name: "f".into(),
            by_pc: StdMap::new(),
        };
        let err = extract_per_sm_blocks(&td, &loc, &sched, true).unwrap_err();
        assert!(
            matches!(
                err,
                ReplayError::Trace(TraceError::AllocationIdMissing { .. })
            ),
            "expected AllocationIdMissing, got {err:?}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn replay_rejects_malformed_global_atomic() {
        assert_replay_rejects_identity(malformed_global_inst(pb::MemoryOpClass::Atomic));
    }

    #[test]
    fn replay_rejects_malformed_ldgsts_source() {
        assert_replay_rejects_identity(malformed_global_inst(pb::MemoryOpClass::AsyncCopy));
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod completeness_tests {
    //! Reader/replay completeness fail-closed on the path replay ACTUALLY
    //! consumes: an incomplete trace lacking a trace_sampling.json sidecar is
    //! E_INCOMPLETE_TRACE; a subset trace passes iff the sidecar's original_grid
    //! matches the launch gridDim (never rewritten) and records.captured matches
    //! records_seen. A lossless-full sidecar may be present, but never sanctions
    //! incomplete coverage.
    use super::*;
    use crate::program::FunctionSchedule;
    use prost::Message;
    use std::collections::BTreeMap as StdMap;

    /// A minimal non-memory record (no memory_op_class) carrying placement, so it
    /// increments records_seen without engaging the allocation-identity gate.
    fn simple_inst() -> pb::Instruction {
        pb::Instruction {
            pc: 16,
            active_mask: Some(0b1),
            predicate_mask: Some(0b1),
            function_unique_id: 1,
            vpc: Some(16),
            sm_id: Some(0),
            warpid_sm: Some(0),
            warpid_tb: Some(0),
            data_width: Some(4),
            memory_op_class: None,
            ..Default::default()
        }
    }

    fn write_grid_trace(
        dir: &std::path::Path,
        grid_x: i32,
        grid_y: i32,
        block_xs: &[i32],
        sidecar: Option<&str>,
    ) {
        let kernel = pb::Kernel {
            id: 1,
            name: "_Z1kv".into(),
            function_unique_id: 1,
            size_shared_memory: 0,
            number_of_registers: 32,
            shared_memory_base_address: 0,
            local_memory_base_address: 0,
            grid_dim: Some(pb::Dim3d {
                x: grid_x,
                y: grid_y,
                z: 1,
            }),
            block_dim: Some(pb::Dim3d { x: 32, y: 1, z: 1 }),
            cluster_dim: Some(pb::Dim3d { x: 1, y: 1, z: 1 }),
        };
        let stream = pb::CudaStream {
            id: 0,
            kernels: vec![kernel],
            ordered_cuda_events: vec![],
        };
        let device = pb::GpuDevice {
            id: 0,
            streams: [(0i64, stream)].into_iter().collect(),
        };
        let trace = pb::Trace {
            name: "m".into(),
            binary_version: 1,
            nvbit_version: "1.8".into(),

        let tb_dir = dir.join("threadblocks/device_0/stream_0/kernel_1");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&tb_dir).unwrap();
        for &bx in block_xs {
            let warp = pb::Warp {
                id: 0,
                instructions: vec![simple_inst()],

    fn minimal_fake_sidecar() -> String {
        format!(
            r#"{{"schema_version":2,"method":"wave_segment_stratified_subset","shape":{{"original_grid":{{"x":60,"y":1,"z":1}}}},"records":{{"captured":12}},"hashes":{{"selected_block_ids_sha256":"{a}","decompressed_payload_sha256":"{a}","sidecar_sha256":"{a}"}},"selection_reconciliation":{{"status":"fixed_point","attempts":1,"max_attempts":3,"capture_stats_sha256":"{a}"}}}}"#,
            a = "a".repeat(64)

    fn rewrite_launch_metadata(
        dir: &std::path::Path,
        kernel_name: Option<&str>,
        block_x: Option<i32>,
    ) {
        let path = dir.join("dynamic_trace.pb");
        let mut trace = pb::Trace::decode(std::fs::read(&path).unwrap().as_slice()).unwrap();
        let kernel = &mut trace
            .gpu_device
            .get_mut(&0)
            .unwrap()
            .streams
            .get_mut(&0)
            .unwrap()
            .kernels[0];
        if let Some(name) = kernel_name {
            kernel.name = name.to_string();
        }
        if let Some(x) = block_x {
            kernel.block_dim.as_mut().unwrap().x = x;
        }
        std::fs::write(path, trace.encode_to_vec()).unwrap();
    }

    fn run(dir: &std::path::Path) -> Result<(), ReplayError> {
        let td = TraceDir::open(dir)?;
        let loc = td.kernels().next().unwrap();
        let sched = FunctionSchedule {
            function_unique_id: 1,
            kernel_name: "_Z1kv".into(),
            function_name: "f".into(),
            by_pc: StdMap::new(),
        };
        extract_per_sm_blocks(&td, &loc, &sched, true).map(|_| ())
    }

    #[test]
    fn complete_trace_no_sidecar_ok() {
        let tmp = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        write_grid_trace(tmp.path(), 4, 1, &[0, 1, 2, 3], None);
        let result = run(tmp.path());
        assert!(result.is_ok(), "{result:?}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn complete_legacy_trace_without_block_dim_needs_no_sampling_binding() {
        let tmp = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        write_grid_trace(tmp.path(), 4, 1, &[0, 1, 2, 3], None);
        let path = tmp.path().join("dynamic_trace.pb");
        let mut trace = pb::Trace::decode(std::fs::read(&path).unwrap().as_slice()).unwrap();
        trace
            .gpu_device
            .get_mut(&0)
            .unwrap()
            .streams
            .get_mut(&0)
            .unwrap()
            .kernels[0]
            .block_dim = None;
        std::fs::write(path, trace.encode_to_vec()).unwrap();
        let result = run(tmp.path());
        assert!(result.is_ok(), "{result:?}");
    }

        let tmp = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();

        let err = run(tmp.path()).unwrap_err();

            matches!(
                err,
                ReplayError::IncompleteTrace {
                    seen: 2,
                    grid_total: 4

            "expected IncompleteTrace, got {err:?}"
        );
    }

    }

        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn minimal_fake_subset_is_rejected_on_consumer_path() {
        let tmp = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let sidecar = minimal_fake_sidecar();
        write_grid_trace(tmp.path(), 60, 1, &SELECTED_BLOCKS, Some(&sidecar));
        let err = run(tmp.path()).unwrap_err();
        assert!(matches!(
            err,
            ReplayError::Trace(TraceError::SamplingSidecarMalformed { .. })
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn bad_seal_block_hash_and_duplicate_membership_are_rejected_on_consumer_path() {
        let valid = payload_bound_subset();
        let cases = [
            valid.replace(r#""captured":12"#, r#""captured":13"#),
            valid.replace(
                "84b7ed43903cca6302ed15cf78ff507c45e575f16d7d5c12c975c5727edc37cf",
                &"0".repeat(64),
            ),
            valid.replace(
                r#"{"id":1,"block_ids":[3,4,5]}"#,
                r#"{"id":1,"block_ids":[2,4,5]}"#,
            ),

        for sidecar in cases {

            write_grid_trace(tmp.path(), 60, 1, &SELECTED_BLOCKS, Some(&sidecar));
            let err = run(tmp.path()).unwrap_err();
            assert!(matches!(
                err,
                ReplayError::Trace(TraceError::SamplingSidecarMalformed { .. })
            ));
        }

            matches!(
                err,
                ReplayError::SelectedBlockMembershipMismatch {
                    seen: 12,
                    declared: 12
                }
            ),
            "got {err:?}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn tampered_payload_is_rejected_before_replay() {
        let tmp = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let sidecar = payload_bound_subset();
        write_grid_trace(tmp.path(), 60, 1, &SELECTED_BLOCKS, Some(&sidecar));
        let path = tmp
            .path()
            .join("threadblocks/device_0/stream_0/kernel_1/d_0_s_0_k_1_0,0,0.pb");
        let mut raw = std::fs::read(&path).unwrap();
        raw[0] ^= 1;
        std::fs::write(path, raw).unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(
            run(tmp.path()).unwrap_err(),
            ReplayError::Trace(TraceError::SamplingSidecarMalformed { .. })
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn sidecar_kernel_and_block_shape_are_bound_to_launch() {

        assert!(matches!(
            run(wrong_block.path()).unwrap_err(),
            ReplayError::BlockDimRewritten { .. }
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn multidim_out_of_grid_cta_is_not_aliased_into_full_coverage() {
        // Grid (2,2,1): CTAs (2,0,0) and (3,0,0) flatten to 2 and 3 (inside
        // [0,4)) but are out of grid on the x axis. They must NOT be accepted as
        // valid blocks (which would falsely satisfy the completeness gate as
        // "4/4 covered"); the shared block_launch_index rejects them typed.
        let tmp = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        write_grid_trace(tmp.path(), 2, 2, &[0, 1, 2, 3], None);
        let err = run(tmp.path()).unwrap_err();
        assert!(
            matches!(
                err,
                ReplayError::Trace(TraceError::BlockIdOutOfRange { .. })
            ),
            "expected BlockIdOutOfRange (not a false full-coverage pass), got {err:?}"
        );
    }
```
