```rust
                warp(1, vec![inst(0)]),
            ],
        }];
        let r = simulate_sm(&blocks, &sched, &params(), None).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(r.instructions_issued, 4);
    }

    #[test]
    fn residency_cap_forces_waves() {
        // Block 0 on sub-cores 0/1, block 1 on sub-cores 2/3 so the
        // uncapped run can use all four sub-cores at once.
        let sched = schedule(vec![
            (0, slot(cb(1), OpClass::Other, "IADD3")),
            (16, slot(cb(1), OpClass::Other, "EXIT")),
        ]);
        let mk_block = |ix: i64, slot0: i32| BlockReplay {
            launch_index: ix,
            warps: vec![
                warp(slot0, vec![inst(0), inst(16)]),
                warp(slot0 + 1, vec![inst(0), inst(16)]),
            ],
        };
        let blocks = vec![mk_block(0, 0), mk_block(1, 2)];
        let mut p = params();
        p.max_resident_warps_per_sm = 2;
        let r = simulate_sm(&blocks, &sched, &p, None).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(r.instructions_issued, 8);
        assert!(r.cycles >= 4, "cycles={}", r.cycles);
        let r2 = simulate_sm(&blocks, &sched, &params(), None).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(r2.cycles, 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn unknown_pc_is_typed_error() {
        let sched = schedule(vec![(0, slot(cb(1), OpClass::Other, "IADD3"))]);
        let blocks = vec![BlockReplay {
            launch_index: 7,
            warps: vec![warp(3, vec![inst(0), inst(999)])],
        }];
        let err = simulate_sm(&blocks, &sched, &params(), None).unwrap_err();
        assert!(matches!(err, IssueError::PcNotInSchedule { pc: 999, .. }));
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // SmCore event-mode (L1Shared) tests: a manual driver stands in for
    // the system layer.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------

    fn shared_core<'a>(
        blocks: &'a [BlockReplay],
        sched: &'a FunctionSchedule,
        p: &IssueModelParams,
    ) -> SmCore<'a> {
        SmCore::new(blocks, sched, p, SmMemMode::L1Shared(l1_config())).unwrap()
    }

    #[test]
    fn shared_mode_miss_blocks_consumer_until_response() {
        let mut load = cb(1);
        load.write_barrier = 0;
        let mut consumer = cb(1);
        consumer.wait_mask = 0b000001;
        let sched = schedule(vec![
            (0, slot(load, OpClass::Other, "LDG.E")),
            (16, slot(consumer, OpClass::Other, "EXIT")),
        ]);
        let blocks = vec![BlockReplay {
            launch_index: 0,
            warps: vec![WarpReplay {
                warp_slot: 0,
                insts: vec![
                    ReplayInst {
                        pc: 0,
                        kind: eligible(0, 1),
                    },
                    inst(16),
                ],
                sectors: vec![0],
            }],
        }];
        let mut core = shared_core(&blocks, &sched, &params());
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        // The load misses → request emitted; the consumer's wait has a
        // PENDING barrier → no computable timer → blocked on response.
        let a = core.advance(u64::MAX, &mut out).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(a, Advance::Idle { wake_at: None });
        assert_eq!(out.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(out[0].issue_time, 0);
        assert_eq!(out[0].source, L2Source::L1Fill);
        let ReplyTo::L1Fill(fill) = out[0].reply else {
            panic!("expected an L1 fill reply");
        };
        // Response at the DRAM arm (423): consumer issues at 423.
        let mut out2 = Vec::new();
        core.on_response(ReplyTo::L1Fill(fill), 423, &mut out2);
        assert!(out2.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(core.advance(u64::MAX, &mut out2).unwrap(), Advance::Done);
        let r = core.result();
        assert_eq!(r.instructions_issued, 2);
        assert_eq!(r.cycles, 424);
    }

    #[test]
    fn shared_mode_horizon_caps_run_ahead_after_a_request() {
        // Independent instructions after a miss: the SM may run ahead,
        // but never past issue_time + l1_miss_latency (the earliest
        // possible response).
        let mut load = cb(1);
        load.write_barrier = 0;
        let sched = schedule(vec![
            (0, slot(load, OpClass::Other, "LDG.E")),
            (16, slot(cb(15), OpClass::Other, "IADD3")),
            (32, slot(cb(15), OpClass::Other, "IADD3")),
            (48, slot(cb(15), OpClass::Other, "EXIT")),
        ]);
        let blocks = vec![BlockReplay {
            launch_index: 0,
            warps: vec![WarpReplay {
                warp_slot: 0,
                insts: vec![
                    ReplayInst {
                        pc: 0,
                        kind: eligible(0, 1),
                    },
                    inst(16),
                    inst(32),
                    inst(48),
                ],
                sectors: vec![0],
            }],
        }];
        let mut core = shared_core(&blocks, &sched, &params());
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        // 4 independent issues would finish at t=46 — well inside the
        // 244-cycle response bound, so the run completes...
        assert_eq!(core.advance(u64::MAX, &mut out).unwrap(), Advance::Done);
        assert_eq!(out.len(), 1);
        // ...but a tight EXTERNAL horizon yields first.
        let blocks2 = vec![BlockReplay {
            launch_index: 0,
            warps: vec![WarpReplay {
                warp_slot: 0,
                insts: vec![
                    ReplayInst {
                        pc: 0,
                        kind: eligible(0, 1),
                    },
                    inst(16),
                    inst(32),
                    inst(48),
                ],
                sectors: vec![0],
            }],
        }];
        let mut core2 = shared_core(&blocks2, &sched, &params());
        let mut out2 = Vec::new();
        let a = core2.advance(10, &mut out2).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            a,
            Advance::Idle { wake_at: Some(10) },
            "the next known timer (16) lies past the horizon: park AT the \
             horizon, where an event may ready an earlier warp"
        );
        assert_eq!(core2.advance(u64::MAX, &mut out2).unwrap(), Advance::Done);
    }

    #[test]
    fn shared_mode_merged_waiters_all_clear_on_one_response() {
        // Two warps load the SAME sector; warp 1 merges into warp 0's
        // fill. Both consumers wait; ONE response clears both.
        let mut load = cb(1);
        load.write_barrier = 0;
        let mut consumer = cb(1);
        consumer.wait_mask = 0b000001;
        let sched = schedule(vec![
            (0, slot(load, OpClass::Other, "LDG.E")),
            (16, slot(consumer, OpClass::Other, "EXIT")),
        ]);
        let mk_warp = |slot_ix: i32| WarpReplay {
            warp_slot: slot_ix,
            insts: vec![
                ReplayInst {
                    pc: 0,
                    kind: eligible(0, 1),
                },
                inst(16),
            ],
            sectors: vec![9],
        };
        let blocks = vec![BlockReplay {
            launch_index: 0,
            warps: vec![mk_warp(0), mk_warp(1)],
        }];
        let mut core = shared_core(&blocks, &sched, &params());
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        assert_eq!(
            core.advance(u64::MAX, &mut out).unwrap(),
            Advance::Idle { wake_at: None }
        );
        assert_eq!(out.len(), 1, "second warp merged, no second request");
        let c = core.l1_counters().unwrap();
        assert_eq!((c.misses, c.merges), (2, 1));
        core.on_response(out[0].reply, 300, &mut out);
        assert_eq!(core.advance(u64::MAX, &mut out).unwrap(), Advance::Done);
        // Both consumers issued at 300 (distinct sub-cores) → cycles 301.
        assert_eq!(core.result().cycles, 301);
    }

    #[test]
    fn shared_mode_mshr_stall_parks_and_retries_on_completion() {
        // MSHR capacity 1: the second warp's DIFFERENT-line load stalls,
        // parks, and retries when the first fill completes.
        let mut load = cb(1);
        load.write_barrier = 0;
        let mut consumer = cb(1);
        consumer.wait_mask = 0b000001;
        let sched = schedule(vec![
            (0, slot(load, OpClass::Other, "LDG.E")),
            (16, slot(consumer, OpClass::Other, "EXIT")),
        ]);
        let blocks = vec![BlockReplay {
            launch_index: 0,
            warps: vec![
                WarpReplay {
                    warp_slot: 0,
                    insts: vec![
                        ReplayInst {
                            pc: 0,
                            kind: eligible(0, 1),
                        },
                        inst(16),
                    ],
                    sectors: vec![0],
                },
                WarpReplay {
                    warp_slot: 1,
                    insts: vec![
                        ReplayInst {
                            pc: 0,
                            kind: eligible(0, 1),
                        },
                        inst(16),
                    ],
                    sectors: vec![8],
                },
            ],
        }];
        let mut cfg = l1_config();
        cfg.mshr_count = Some(1);
        let mut core = SmCore::new(&blocks, &sched, &params(), SmMemMode::L1Shared(cfg)).unwrap();
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        assert_eq!(
            core.advance(u64::MAX, &mut out).unwrap(),
            Advance::Idle { wake_at: None }
        );
        assert_eq!(out.len(), 1, "second load stalled, not requested");
        assert_eq!(core.l1_counters().unwrap().stall_events, 1);
        // First fill completes → retry emits the parked request at 244.
        let first = out[0].reply;
        out.clear();
        core.on_response(first, 244, &mut out);
        assert_eq!(out.len(), 1, "retry sent the parked sector");
        assert_eq!(out[0].issue_time, 244);
        assert_eq!(
            core.advance(u64::MAX, &mut out).unwrap(),
            Advance::Idle { wake_at: None }
        );
        let second = out[0].reply;
        core.on_response(second, 488, &mut out);
        assert_eq!(core.advance(u64::MAX, &mut out).unwrap(), Advance::Done);
        let r = core.result();
        assert_eq!(r.instructions_issued, 4);
        // Warp 1's consumer issues at 488 → cycles 489.
        assert_eq!(r.cycles, 489);
    }

    #[test]
    fn shared_mode_bypass_load_waits_on_direct_reply() {
        let mut load = cb(1);
        load.write_barrier = 2;
        let mut consumer = cb(1);
        consumer.wait_mask = 0b000100;
        let sched = schedule(vec![
            (0, slot(load, OpClass::Other, "LDG.E.CG")),
            (16, slot(consumer, OpClass::Other, "EXIT")),
        ]);
        let blocks = vec![BlockReplay {
            launch_index: 0,
            warps: vec![WarpReplay {
                warp_slot: 0,
                insts: vec![
                    ReplayInst {
                        pc: 0,
                        kind: AccessKind::GlobalBypass {
                            off: 0,
                            len: 2,
                            token: CacheOpToken::LdgECg,
                        },
                    },
                    inst(16),
                ],
                sectors: vec![40, 41],
            }],
        }];
        let mut core = shared_core(&blocks, &sched, &params());
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        assert_eq!(
            core.advance(u64::MAX, &mut out).unwrap(),
            Advance::Idle { wake_at: None }
        );
        assert_eq!(out.len(), 2, "one request per bypass sector");
        assert!(out.iter().all(|r| r.source == L2Source::Bypass));
        assert!(
            out.iter().all(|r| r.class == L2OpClass::Read),
            ".cg bypass loads are read-class at the L2"
        );
        assert!(matches!(
            out[0].reply,
            ReplyTo::Warp {
                warp: 0,
                barrier: 2
            }
        ));
        // Both responses must land before the wait clears.
        let mut sink = Vec::new();
        core.on_response(out[0].reply, 244, &mut sink);
        assert_eq!(
            core.advance(u64::MAX, &mut sink).unwrap(),
            Advance::Idle { wake_at: None },
            "one of two pending units still outstanding"
        );
        core.on_response(out[1].reply, 423, &mut sink);
        assert_eq!(core.advance(u64::MAX, &mut sink).unwrap(), Advance::Done);
        assert_eq!(core.result().cycles, 424);
    }

    #[test]
    fn shared_mode_store_emits_mutation_only_requests() {
        let sched = schedule(vec![
            (0, slot(cb(1), OpClass::Other, "STG.E")),
            (16, slot(cb(1), OpClass::Other, "EXIT")),
        ]);
        let blocks = vec![BlockReplay {
            launch_index: 0,
            warps: vec![WarpReplay {
                warp_slot: 0,
                insts: vec![
                    ReplayInst {
                        pc: 0,
                        kind: AccessKind::GlobalStore { off: 0, len: 2 },
                    },
                    inst(16),
                ],
                sectors: vec![100, 101],
            }],
        }];
        let mut core = shared_core(&blocks, &sched, &params());
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        assert_eq!(core.advance(u64::MAX, &mut out).unwrap(), Advance::Done);
        assert_eq!(out.len(), 2);
        assert!(out.iter().all(|r| r.source == L2Source::Store
            && r.class == L2OpClass::WriteAtomic
            && r.reply == ReplyTo::None));
    }

    /// §6.4 slice 2 — one instruction's cold 4-sector line miss reaches
    /// the L2 as ONE request CARRYING ALL FOUR SECTORS (the merged
    /// sectors fold into the fill's mask; NCU counts 4 LTS sectors),
    /// with a single response completing every waiter.
    #[test]
    fn shared_mode_line_fill_folds_batch_sectors_into_one_request() {
        let mut load = cb(1);
        load.write_barrier = 2;
        let mut consumer = cb(1);
        consumer.wait_mask = 0b000100;
        let sched = schedule(vec![
            (0, slot(load, OpClass::Other, "LDG.E")),
            (16, slot(consumer, OpClass::Other, "EXIT")),
        ]);
        let blocks = vec![BlockReplay {
            launch_index: 0,
            warps: vec![WarpReplay {
                warp_slot: 0,
                insts: vec![
                    ReplayInst {
                        pc: 0,
                        kind: AccessKind::GlobalEligible {
                            off: 0,
                            len: 4,
                            token: CacheOpToken::LdgECa,
                        },
                    },
                    inst(16),
                ],
                sectors: vec![40, 41, 42, 43],
            }],
        }];
        let mut core = shared_core(&blocks, &sched, &params());
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        assert_eq!(
            core.advance(u64::MAX, &mut out).unwrap(),
            Advance::Idle { wake_at: None }
        );
        assert_eq!(out.len(), 1, "one L2 transaction for the whole line");
        assert_eq!(out[0].sector_mask, 0b1111);
        assert_eq!(out[0].reply, ReplyTo::L1Fill(FillKey::Line(10)));
        let mut sink = Vec::new();
        core.on_response(out[0].reply, 244, &mut sink);
        assert_eq!(core.advance(u64::MAX, &mut sink).unwrap(), Advance::Done);
        assert_eq!(core.result().cycles, 245);
    }

    /// §6.4 slice 2 — a LATER instruction merging onto an in-flight
    /// line fill: a NEW sector sends a follow-up `ReplyTo::None` fetch
    /// (the L2 must see it once), a re-touched sector sends nothing
    /// (MSHR merge), and every waiter still rides the ORIGINAL fill's
    /// one response.
    #[test]
    fn shared_mode_same_batch_cross_instruction_merge_folds() {
        // Gate fix 2026-07-07: fold scope is the EMISSION BATCH (one
        // advance call), not one instruction — a later instruction's
        // merge onto an earlier instruction's line fill folds into that
        // request's mask (so worst-of-mask pricing covers it) instead
        // of splitting off a follow-up fetch.
        let mut load_a = cb(1);
        load_a.write_barrier = 2;
        let mut load_b = cb(1);
        load_b.write_barrier = 2;
        let mut consumer = cb(1);
        consumer.wait_mask = 0b000100;
        let sched = schedule(vec![
            (0, slot(load_a, OpClass::Other, "LDG.E")),
            (16, slot(load_b, OpClass::Other, "LDG.E")),
            (32, slot(consumer, OpClass::Other, "EXIT")),
        ]);
        let blocks = vec![BlockReplay {
            launch_index: 0,
            warps: vec![WarpReplay {
                warp_slot: 0,
                insts: vec![
                    ReplayInst {
                        pc: 0,
                        kind: AccessKind::GlobalEligible {
                            off: 0,
                            len: 1,
                            token: CacheOpToken::LdgECa,
                        },
                    },
                    ReplayInst {
                        pc: 16,
                        kind: AccessKind::GlobalEligible {
                            off: 1,
                            len: 2,
                            token: CacheOpToken::LdgECa,
                        },
                    },
                    inst(32),
                ],
                // A: sector 40. B: sector 41 (folds) + 40 (re-touch).
                sectors: vec![40, 41, 40],
            }],
        }];
        let mut core = shared_core(&blocks, &sched, &params());
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        assert_eq!(
            core.advance(u64::MAX, &mut out).unwrap(),
            Advance::Idle { wake_at: None }
        );
        assert_eq!(out.len(), 1, "one line transaction for the whole batch");
        assert_eq!(out[0].sector_mask, 0b11, "B's sector folded into A's fill");
        assert_eq!(out[0].reply, ReplyTo::L1Fill(FillKey::Line(10)));
        let mut sink = Vec::new();
        core.on_response(out[0].reply, 244, &mut sink);
        assert_eq!(
            core.advance(u64::MAX, &mut sink).unwrap(),
            Advance::Done,
            "one response clears both instructions' waiters"
        );
    }

    /// A merge onto a fill emitted in an EARLIER batch (the request
    /// already left with the SM's previous yield) cannot fold — it
    /// sends exactly one follow-up `ReplyTo::None` fetch, and the
    /// waiter still rides the original fill's response.
    #[test]
    fn shared_mode_cross_batch_merge_sends_followup_fetch_once() {
        let mut load_m = cb(1);
        load_m.write_barrier = 2;
        let mut load_l = cb(1);
        load_l.write_barrier = 3;
        // Merging load: gated on barrier 2 (fill M's return) so it
        // issues in a LATER advance call while fill L is still in
        // flight; its own waiter registers on barrier 2.
        let mut load_merge = cb(1);
        load_merge.write_barrier = 2;
        load_merge.wait_mask = 0b000100;
        let mut consumer = cb(1);
        consumer.wait_mask = 0b001100;
        let sched = schedule(vec![
            (0, slot(load_m, OpClass::Other, "LDG.E")),
            (16, slot(load_l, OpClass::Other, "LDG.E")),
            (32, slot(load_merge, OpClass::Other, "LDG.E")),
            (48, slot(consumer, OpClass::Other, "EXIT")),
        ]);
        let blocks = vec![BlockReplay {
            launch_index: 0,
            warps: vec![WarpReplay {
                warp_slot: 0,
                insts: vec![
                    ReplayInst {
                        pc: 0,
                        kind: AccessKind::GlobalEligible {
                            off: 0,
                            len: 1,
                            token: CacheOpToken::LdgECa,
                        },
                    },
                    ReplayInst {
                        pc: 16,
                        kind: AccessKind::GlobalEligible {
                            off: 1,
                            len: 1,
                            token: CacheOpToken::LdgECa,
                        },
                    },
                    ReplayInst {
                        pc: 32,
                        kind: AccessKind::GlobalEligible {
                            off: 2,
                            len: 1,
                            token: CacheOpToken::LdgECa,
                        },
                    },
                    inst(48),
                ],
                // M: sector 80 (line 20). L: sector 40 (line 10).
                // Merge: sector 41 (line 10, new sector).
                sectors: vec![80, 40, 41],
            }],
        }];
        let mut core = shared_core(&blocks, &sched, &params());
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        assert_eq!(
            core.advance(u64::MAX, &mut out).unwrap(),
            Advance::Idle { wake_at: None }
        );
        assert_eq!(out.len(), 2, "two fills; the merging load is gated");
        assert_eq!(out[0].reply, ReplyTo::L1Fill(FillKey::Line(20)));
        assert_eq!(out[1].reply, ReplyTo::L1Fill(FillKey::Line(10)));
        assert_eq!(out[1].sector_mask, 0b01);
        // Fill M returns; the merging load issues in a NEW batch while
        // fill L is still in flight.
        let mut out2 = Vec::new();
        core.on_response(out[0].reply, 423, &mut out2);
        assert_eq!(
            core.advance(u64::MAX, &mut out2).unwrap(),
            Advance::Idle { wake_at: None }
        );
        assert_eq!(out2.len(), 1, "exactly one follow-up fetch");
        assert_eq!(out2[0].sector_mask, 0b10, "only the new sector");
        assert_eq!(out2[0].reply, ReplyTo::None, "no second response");
        assert_eq!(out2[0].source, L2Source::L1Fill);
        // Fill L's one response clears BOTH its own waiter (barrier 3)
        // and the merged load's waiter (barrier 2).
        let mut sink = Vec::new();
        core.on_response(out[1].reply, 846, &mut sink);
        assert_eq!(core.advance(u64::MAX, &mut sink).unwrap(), Advance::Done);
    }

    /// ATOM records ride BYPASS provenance (they never stage into the
    /// modeled L1) but carry the §6.4 WRITE class at the L2: the source
    /// says who sent the sector, the class says how it hits.
    #[test]
    fn shared_mode_atom_is_bypass_provenance_write_class() {
        let mut atom = cb(1);
        atom.write_barrier = 2;
        let mut consumer = cb(1);
        consumer.wait_mask = 0b000100;
        let sched = schedule(vec![
            (0, slot(atom, OpClass::Other, "ATOMG.E.ADD.STRONG.GPU")),
            (16, slot(consumer, OpClass::Other, "EXIT")),
        ]);
        let blocks = vec![BlockReplay {
            launch_index: 0,
            warps: vec![WarpReplay {
                warp_slot: 0,
                insts: vec![
                    ReplayInst {
                        pc: 0,
                        kind: AccessKind::GlobalBypass {
                            off: 0,
                            len: 1,
                            token: CacheOpToken::Atom,
                        },
                    },
                    inst(16),
                ],
                sectors: vec![40],
            }],
        }];
        let mut core = shared_core(&blocks, &sched, &params());
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        assert_eq!(
            core.advance(u64::MAX, &mut out).unwrap(),
            Advance::Idle { wake_at: None }
        );
        assert_eq!(out.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(out[0].source, L2Source::Bypass);
        assert_eq!(out[0].class, L2OpClass::WriteAtomic);
        assert!(
            matches!(
                out[0].reply,
                ReplyTo::Warp {
                    warp: 0,
                    barrier: 2
                }
            ),
            "the atomic's return value still waits on the reply"
        );
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Shared L2 slice model — a lockstep port of the sectored set-associative
//! replay core in `tools/cache_replay/sector_cache_replay.py`
//! (`replay_access_stream` + `_install_way`), the engine behind the
//! Phase-1 L2 predictor. Like the L1 port, only the CACHE STATE MACHINE
//! is taken: the Python module replayed a timeless trace-order stream,
//! while the sim drives this model with the globally (time, seq)-ordered
//! request stream the event engine produces — the ordering the flat
//! replay stood in for.
//!
//! Ported semantics (32 B sectors in 128 B lines) — these bullets
//! describe the READ class, the rule the Python engine implements; the
//! §6.4 [`L2OpClass::WriteAtomic`] class additionally hits on line-TAG
//! residency alone (same state trajectory, different counting — see
//! `L2OpClass`; the parity corpus pins the Read class only):
//! - a Read-class sector access HITS iff its line tag is resident in
//!   the addressed set AND that sector's valid bit is set;
//! - a resident line whose requested sector is not yet valid is a
//!   sector-fill miss for reads (the bit is set immediately — the
//!   Python replay is occupancy-only, fills are not in-flight at this
//!   level) and a tag-match HIT for writes/atomics;
//! - a non-resident line allocates a way, evicting per policy when the
//!   set is full (LRU / SRRIP 2-bit RRPV / deterministic BIP 1-in-32);
//! - slice/set addressing: `slice = hash(line_id)`,
//!   `set = (line_id // num_slices) % num_sets_per_slice`, with the six
//!   pre-registered slice-hash candidates ported bit-exactly.
//!
//! Rule 1 note: the Phase-1 calibrator SELECTED a config for sm_86 by
//! fitting against local NCU labels (capacity_scale, hash, policy). That
//! selection is a label-fitted artifact and is deliberately NOT consumed
//! here. The sim's geometry comes from the arch card's vendor-documented
//! `l2_geometry` (capacity, line/sector, slice count); associativity,
//! slice hash and replacement policy are DOCUMENTED-DEFAULT hypothesis
//! knobs below (same fail-closed pattern as the L1 MSHR default), to be
//! closed by microbenchmarks — never by label fits.
//!
//! MSHR/fill timing: v0 models L2 occupancy only (no L2-level MSHR or
//! in-flight fill state). The L1's MSHRs already bound the per-SM
//! outstanding stream, and the Python reference has no L2 fill model to
//! port — an L2 MSHR would be an uncarded invention at this point.

/// Number of 32 B sectors per 128 B line (fixed physical granularity;
/// the `u8` way masks below hold exactly these four bits).
pub const L2_SECTORS_PER_LINE: u32 = 4;

/// Documented-default L2 associativity (research gap on every card):
/// 16 ways is the Accel-Sim Ampere config family's value and the common
/// literature assumption for NVIDIA L2s; not microbenched on this
/// project's cards yet. Same contract as the L1 MSHR default: a
/// documented hypothesis knob, never a silent invention.
pub const DOCUMENTED_DEFAULT_L2_ASSOCIATIVITY: u32 = 16;

/// The six pre-registered slice-hash candidates, ported bit-exactly from
/// `SLICE_HASH_REGISTRY`. The card records only the slice COUNT
/// (vendor-documented); which hash the crossbar uses is a research gap.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum SliceHash {
    /// Documented-default candidate (v0 approximation).
    LineMod,
    SectorMod,
    XorFolded,
    KnuthMult,
    ShiftMod,
    BitReverse,
}

/// Documented-default slice hash: plain line-interleaving. The Python
/// registry existed to CALIBRATE this unknown; v0 pins the simplest
/// candidate and records it as an approximation.
pub const DOCUMENTED_DEFAULT_L2_SLICE_HASH: SliceHash = SliceHash::LineMod;

impl SliceHash {
    /// `slice_id` for a 128 B line address. Lockstep with the Python
    /// registry functions, INCLUDING negative line ids: Python's `%` is
    /// floored (→ `rem_euclid`), `>>` on negatives is an arithmetic
    /// shift, and `& 0xFFFF…` of a negative yields its two's-complement
    /// low bits — all matched here so a wire-admitted negative address
    /// (a `base_delta` stream summing below zero is structurally legal)
    /// replays identically instead of wrapping through `u64`.
    /// Pinned-value tests below cover both signs.
    pub fn slice_of(self, line_id: i64, num_slices: u32) -> u32 {
        let n = i64::from(num_slices);
        let s = match self {
            SliceHash::LineMod => line_id.rem_euclid(n),
            // (line * 4) % n == ((line %e n) * 4) % n — overflow-free
            // and sign-correct under the euclidean remainder.
            SliceHash::SectorMod => {
                (line_id.rem_euclid(n) * i64::from(L2_SECTORS_PER_LINE)).rem_euclid(n)
            }
            SliceHash::XorFolded => (line_id ^ (line_id >> 5) ^ (line_id >> 11)).rem_euclid(n),
            // Knuth multiplicative hash masked to the low 32 bits — the
            // wrapping product's low bits equal Python's full-precision
            // product masked (two's complement, both signs).
            SliceHash::KnuthMult => {
                (line_id.wrapping_mul(2_654_435_761) & 0xFFFF_FFFF).rem_euclid(n)
            }
            SliceHash::ShiftMod => (line_id >> 1).rem_euclid(n),
            SliceHash::BitReverse => i64::from((line_id as u16).reverse_bits()).rem_euclid(n),
        };
        s as u32
    }
}

/// Replacement policy. LRU is the documented-default approximation (the
/// same status as the L1 pool's LRU); SRRIP/BIP are ported so the
/// lockstep differential covers the full Python surface and calibration
/// can flip the knob later without a re-port.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum L2Replacement {
    Lru,
    Srrip,
    Bip,
}

pub const DOCUMENTED_DEFAULT_L2_REPLACEMENT: L2Replacement = L2Replacement::Lru;

const SRRIP_RRPV_MAX: i64 = 3;
const SRRIP_INSERT_RRPV: i64 = 2;
const BIP_MRU_INSERT_PERIOD: u64 = 32;

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum L2ConfigError {
    #[error("capacity_bytes {capacity} must be >= line_bytes {line}")]
    CapacityBelowLine { capacity: u64, line: u32 },
    #[error(
        "line/sector geometry must be 128/32 (got line={line}, sector={sector}) — the way masks are 4-bit"
    )]
    UnsupportedGranularity { line: u32, sector: u32 },
    #[error("associativity must be >= 1")]
    AssociativityZero,
    #[error("num_slices must be >= 1")]
    SlicesZero,
    #[error(
        "arch {arch:?} has not reviewed the documented-default L2 knobs (assoc 16/LRU/line_mod \
         were reviewed for sm_86 only) — card the fields or extend the reviewed set deliberately"
    )]
    DefaultsUnreviewedForArch { arch: String },
    #[error(
        "card l2_geometry.policy is absent — the model write-allocates stores, and a card \
         without a measured policy must fail closed, never assume write-allocate"
    )]
    WritePolicyGap,
    #[error(
        "card l2_geometry.policy {policy:?} is not a write-allocate token this model implements"
    )]
    WritePolicyUnsupported { policy: String },
}

/// Arches whose documented-default L2 knobs (associativity 16, LRU,
/// line_mod) have been REVIEWED against available public evidence.
/// Same per-arch-set pattern as `cache_op::BARE_LDG_E_DEFAULTS_TO_CA`:
/// an unreviewed arch fails closed instead of inheriting another
/// arch's hypotheses (CLAUDE.md architecture-coupling discipline).
pub const L2_DEFAULTS_REVIEWED_ARCHES: [&str; 1] = ["sm_86"];

/// The one write policy the store path implements (stores allocate in
/// L2 like loads). Cards carrying anything else — or nothing — fail
/// closed at construction.
pub const L2_WRITE_ALLOCATE_POLICY: &str = "write_allocate_non_inclusive";

/// L2 geometry + policy. Construct via [`L2Config::from_carded_geometry`]
/// so the documented-default provenance is explicit at the call site.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct L2Config {
    pub capacity_bytes: u64,
    pub line_bytes: u32,
    pub sector_bytes: u32,
    pub num_slices: u32,
    pub associativity: u32,
    pub replacement: L2Replacement,
    pub slice_hash: SliceHash,
}

impl L2Config {
    /// Config from the arch card's vendor-documented `l2_geometry` block,
    /// with the three research-gap fields taking their DOCUMENTED
    /// defaults (associativity 16 / LRU / line-interleaved slices) —
    /// only on arches that have REVIEWED those defaults, and only when
    /// the card's write `policy` is one the store model implements
    /// (`None` is a typed gap per the sim-calib `L2Geometry.policy`
    /// contract, never an implicit write-allocate).
    pub fn from_carded_geometry(
        arch_token: &str,
        capacity_bytes: u64,
        line_bytes: u32,
        sector_bytes: u32,
        num_slices: u32,
        policy: Option<&str>,
    ) -> Result<Self, L2ConfigError> {
        if !L2_DEFAULTS_REVIEWED_ARCHES.contains(&arch_token) {
            return Err(L2ConfigError::DefaultsUnreviewedForArch {
                arch: arch_token.to_owned(),
            });
        }
        match policy {
            None => return Err(L2ConfigError::WritePolicyGap),
            Some(L2_WRITE_ALLOCATE_POLICY) => {}
            Some(other) => {
                return Err(L2ConfigError::WritePolicyUnsupported {
                    policy: other.to_owned(),
                });
            }
        }
        let cfg = Self {
            capacity_bytes,
            line_bytes,
            sector_bytes,
            num_slices,
            associativity: DOCUMENTED_DEFAULT_L2_ASSOCIATIVITY,
            replacement: DOCUMENTED_DEFAULT_L2_REPLACEMENT,
            slice_hash: DOCUMENTED_DEFAULT_L2_SLICE_HASH,
        };
        cfg.validate()?;
        Ok(cfg)
    }

    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), L2ConfigError> {
        if self.line_bytes != 128 || self.sector_bytes != 32 {
            return Err(L2ConfigError::UnsupportedGranularity {
                line: self.line_bytes,
                sector: self.sector_bytes,
            });
        }
        if self.capacity_bytes < u64::from(self.line_bytes) {
            return Err(L2ConfigError::CapacityBelowLine {
                capacity: self.capacity_bytes,
                line: self.line_bytes,
            });
        }
        if self.associativity == 0 {
            return Err(L2ConfigError::AssociativityZero);
        }
        if self.num_slices == 0 {
            return Err(L2ConfigError::SlicesZero);
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// `max(1, capacity // line)` — Python `total_lines`.
    pub fn total_lines(&self) -> u64 {
        (self.capacity_bytes / u64::from(self.line_bytes)).max(1)
    }

    /// `max(1, max(1, total_lines // num_slices) // associativity)` —
    /// Python `num_sets_per_slice`.
    pub fn num_sets_per_slice(&self) -> u64 {
        (self.total_lines() / u64::from(self.num_slices))
            .max(1)
            .checked_div(u64::from(self.associativity))
            .expect("associativity validated nonzero")
            .max(1)
    }
}

/// Who put the sector on the L2 stream. PROVENANCE ONLY: carried on
/// requests for the system layer's emission observer — the cache model
/// itself never consumes it (gate-3 altitude note: emission accounting
/// lives OUTSIDE the models). The BEHAVIORAL per-access dimension is
/// [`L2OpClass`], carried separately: source is 4-way who-sent-it,
/// class is 2-way how-it-hits (an ATOM rides `Bypass` provenance with
/// `WriteAtomic` class).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum L2Source {
    /// An L1 fill request (line-allocation or resident-sector fetch).
    L1Fill,
    /// A manifest-ineligible load sector bypassing the L1 (.cg/.cs/…).
    Bypass,
    /// A global-class sector whose pc the classifier did not tag.
    Untagged,
    /// A global store sector (card policy `write_allocate_non_inclusive`
    /// → stores allocate in L2 exactly like loads).
    Store,
}

/// Behavioral ACCESS CLASS of one L2 sector access — the §6.4
/// per-access-class hit rule. NCU's `lts__t_sectors_lookup_hit`
/// accounting is hypothesized to be per-op-class (gate-3 error
/// attribution, validated on the histogram witness cell): a LOAD needs
/// the sector's DATA, so it hits only when the sector's valid bit is set
/// (the ported Python rule); a WRITE/ATOMIC/REDUCTION carries its own
/// data and coalesces into any resident line, so its lookup hits on
/// line-TAG residency alone. This is a COUNTING rule, not per-cell
/// tuning: the cache state trajectory is identical either way (a
/// write-class access to a resident line validates the sector exactly
/// as the sector-fill-miss path did).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum L2OpClass {
    /// Load-class sector (L1 fills, bypass loads, untagged, LDGSTS):
    /// hit iff the sector's valid bit is set.
    Read,
    /// Store/atomic/reduction sector (STG, RED, ATOM): hit iff the line
    /// TAG is resident, regardless of the sector's valid bit.
    WriteAtomic,
}

/// Outcome of one L2 sector access. `counted_hit` is the observation
/// (per-class NCU accounting, drives [`L2Counters`] and the driver's
/// emission observer); `sector_present` is the physics (the requested
/// sector's data was resident BEFORE this access — the response-pricing
/// arm: a tag-match write COUNTS as a hit but a dependent atomic reply
/// still fetches absent data from DRAM). For `Read` the two coincide.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct L2Outcome {
    pub counted_hit: bool,
    pub sector_present: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct L2Counters {
    pub hits: u64,
    pub misses: u64,
    /// Miss split (state-machine kinds, not the Python 3C diagnostic).
    pub line_misses: u64,
    pub sector_fill_misses: u64,
    /// Of `hits`: write-class hits granted on line-TAG residency while
    /// the sector's valid bit was still clear (the §6.4 rule's whole
    /// contribution — zero when every access is `Read`-class).
    pub write_tag_hits: u64,
}

impl L2Counters {
    pub fn add(&mut self, other: &L2Counters) {
        self.hits += other.hits;
        self.misses += other.misses;
        self.line_misses += other.line_misses;
        self.sector_fill_misses += other.sector_fill_misses;
        self.write_tag_hits += other.write_tag_hits;
    }

    pub fn total(&self) -> u64 {
        self.hits + self.misses
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
struct Way {
    /// Full line id as the tag (signed: negative wire-admitted ids
    /// replay with Python's floored semantics, never wrapped).
    tag: i64,
    /// Valid-sector bitmask (bit = sector index within the line, 0..4).
    mask: u8,
    /// LRU timestamp (LRU/BIP — BIP inserts can go BELOW the current
    /// minimum, hence signed) or RRPV (SRRIP).
    recency: i64,
}

/// The shared L2: one state machine partitioned into `num_slices ×
/// num_sets_per_slice` sets. Timeless by design — the caller (the event
/// system) presents accesses in the globally ordered request stream.
pub struct L2Model {
    cfg: L2Config,
    num_sets: u64,
    sets: Vec<Vec<Way>>,
    clock: i64,
    bip_counter: u64,
    pub counters: L2Counters,
}

impl L2Model {
    pub fn new(cfg: L2Config) -> Result<Self, L2ConfigError> {
        cfg.validate()?;
        let num_sets = cfg.num_sets_per_slice();
        let n = usize::try_from(u64::from(cfg.num_slices) * num_sets)
            .expect("set count fits usize on 64-bit targets");
        Ok(Self {
            cfg,
            num_sets,
            sets: vec![Vec::new(); n],
            clock: 0,
            bip_counter: 0,
            counters: L2Counters::default(),
        })
    }

    pub fn config(&self) -> &L2Config {
        &self.cfg
    }

    /// One 32 B sector access in global request order. `line_id` is the
    /// global 128 B line address (`sector_id >> 2` in the L1's sector-id
    /// space); negative ids (wire-admissible) take Python's floored
    /// division/remainder. The STATE trajectory is identical for both
    /// [`L2OpClass`]es — the class only changes how a resident-line /
    /// invalid-sector access is COUNTED (Read: sector-fill miss, the
    /// ported Python rule; WriteAtomic: tag-match hit).
    pub fn access(&mut self, line_id: i64, sector: u8, class: L2OpClass) -> L2Outcome {
        debug_assert!(sector < 4);
        let line = line_id;
        let sbit = 1u8 << sector;
        let slice = u64::from(self.cfg.slice_hash.slice_of(line, self.cfg.num_slices));
        let set_idx = line
            .div_euclid(i64::from(self.cfg.num_slices))
            .rem_euclid(self.num_sets as i64) as u64;
        let set_key = usize::try_from(slice * self.num_sets + set_idx)
            .expect("set key fits usize on 64-bit targets");
        self.clock += 1;

        let policy = self.cfg.replacement;
        let ways = &mut self.sets[set_key];
        if let Some(way) = ways.iter_mut().find(|w| w.tag == line) {
            let resident_hit = way.mask & sbit != 0;
            way.recency = match policy {
                L2Replacement::Srrip => 0,
                _ => self.clock,
            };
            if resident_hit {
                self.counters.hits += 1;
                return L2Outcome {
                    counted_hit: true,
                    sector_present: true,
                };
            }
            // Line resident, sector not yet valid: the write-class
            // access supplies its own data → tag-match hit; the read
            // needs the data → sector-fill miss. Both validate the bit.
            way.mask |= sbit;
            return match class {
                L2OpClass::WriteAtomic => {
                    self.counters.hits += 1;
                    self.counters.write_tag_hits += 1;
                    L2Outcome {
                        counted_hit: true,
                        sector_present: false,
                    }
                }
                L2OpClass::Read => {
                    self.counters.misses += 1;
                    self.counters.sector_fill_misses += 1;
                    L2Outcome {
                        counted_hit: false,
                        sector_present: false,
                    }
                }
            };
        }
        // Line miss → allocate (evicting per policy when the set is
        // full). A miss for BOTH classes: no tag to match.
        install_way(
            ways,
            line,
            sbit,
            self.cfg.associativity,
            policy,
            self.clock,
            self.bip_counter,
        );
        if policy == L2Replacement::Bip {
            self.bip_counter += 1;
        }
        self.counters.misses += 1;
        self.counters.line_misses += 1;
        L2Outcome {
            counted_hit: false,
            sector_present: false,
        }
    }
}

/// `_install_way` port: insert a freshly-fetched line, evicting per
/// policy when the set is full.
fn install_way(
    ways: &mut Vec<Way>,
    tag: i64,
    sbit: u8,
    assoc: u32,
    policy: L2Replacement,
    clock: i64,
    bip_counter: u64,
) {
    if ways.len() < assoc as usize {
        let recency = match policy {
            L2Replacement::Srrip => SRRIP_INSERT_RRPV,
            L2Replacement::Bip => {
                let mru = bip_counter.is_multiple_of(BIP_MRU_INSERT_PERIOD);
                if mru || ways.is_empty() {
                    clock
                } else {
                    min_recency(ways) - 1
                }
            }
            L2Replacement::Lru => clock,
        };
        ways.push(Way {
            tag,
            mask: sbit,
            recency,
        });
        return;
    }

    if policy == L2Replacement::Srrip {
        // Find a way at RRPV max; if none, age all until one reaches it.
        loop {
            if let Some(w) = ways.iter_mut().find(|w| w.recency >= SRRIP_RRPV_MAX) {
                *w = Way {
                    tag,
                    mask: sbit,
                    recency: SRRIP_INSERT_RRPV,
                };
                return;
            }
            for w in ways.iter_mut() {
                w.recency += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    // LRU / BIP eviction: least recency wins (first index on ties, like
    // the Python strict `<` scan).
    let victim = ways
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .min_by_key(|(ix, w)| (w.recency, *ix))
        .map(|(ix, _)| ix)
        .expect("set is full, hence non-empty");
    let recency = match policy {
        L2Replacement::Bip => {
            let mru = bip_counter.is_multiple_of(BIP_MRU_INSERT_PERIOD);
            if mru { clock } else { min_recency(ways) - 1 }
        }
        _ => clock,
    };
    ways[victim] = Way {
        tag,
        mask: sbit,
        recency,
    };
}

fn min_recency(ways: &[Way]) -> i64 {
    ways.iter()
        .map(|w| w.recency)
        .min()
        .expect("min_recency on non-empty ways")
}

#[cfg(test)]
#[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// Read-class access sugar: the ported Python rule, where the
    /// counted hit and the physical sector presence coincide.
    fn rd(l2: &mut L2Model, line: i64, sector: u8) -> bool {
        l2.access(line, sector, L2OpClass::Read).counted_hit
    }

    /// Write-class access sugar (STG/RED/ATOM): counted hit under the
    /// §6.4 tag-match rule.
    fn wr(l2: &mut L2Model, line: i64, sector: u8) -> bool {
        l2.access(line, sector, L2OpClass::WriteAtomic).counted_hit
    }

    fn cfg(capacity: u64, assoc: u32, slices: u32) -> L2Config {
        L2Config {
            capacity_bytes: capacity,
            line_bytes: 128,
            sector_bytes: 32,
            num_slices: slices,
            associativity: assoc,
            replacement: L2Replacement::Lru,
            slice_hash: SliceHash::LineMod,
        }
    }

    /// Pinned against the Python registry (`SLICE_HASH_REGISTRY`) for
    /// lines {0, 1, 5, 12345, 987654321, 2^40+7, 2^56+123} at 6 and 7
    /// slices — regenerated verbatim from `sector_cache_replay.py`.
    #[test]
    fn slice_hashes_match_python_pins() {
        let lines: [i64; 7] = [0, 1, 5, 12345, 987_654_321, (1 << 40) + 7, (1 << 56) + 123];
        let cases: [(SliceHash, [u32; 7], [u32; 7]); 6] = [
            (
                SliceHash::LineMod,
                [0, 1, 5, 3, 3, 5, 1],
                [0, 1, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1],
            ),
            (
                SliceHash::SectorMod,
                [0, 4, 2, 0, 0, 2, 4],
                [0, 4, 6, 2, 5, 1, 4],
            ),
            (
                SliceHash::XorFolded,
                [0, 1, 5, 2, 5, 3, 2],
                [0, 1, 5, 1, 4, 3, 0],
            ),
            (
                SliceHash::KnuthMult,
                [0, 1, 5, 3, 3, 3, 5],
                [0, 5, 6, 3, 3, 5, 3],
            ),
            (
                SliceHash::ShiftMod,
                [0, 0, 2, 4, 4, 5, 3],
                [0, 0, 2, 5, 1, 4, 0],
            ),
            (
                SliceHash::BitReverse,
                [0, 2, 4, 0, 4, 2, 0],
                [0, 1, 3, 6, 5, 0, 6],
            ),
        ];
        for (hash, at6, at7) in cases {
            for (i, &line) in lines.iter().enumerate() {
                assert_eq!(hash.slice_of(line, 6), at6[i], "{hash:?}({line}, 6)");
                assert_eq!(hash.slice_of(line, 7), at7[i], "{hash:?}({line}, 7)");
            }
        }
    }

    /// NEGATIVE line ids (wire-admissible via base_delta streams summing
    /// below zero) must replay with Python's floored semantics, never a
    /// u64 wrap — pins regenerated from `sector_cache_replay.py` for
    /// lines {-1, -93, -12345, -(2^40)-7}.
    #[test]
    fn negative_line_ids_match_python_floored_semantics() {
        let lines: [i64; 4] = [-1, -93, -12345, -(1 << 40) - 7];
        let cases: [(SliceHash, [u32; 4], [u32; 4]); 6] = [
            (SliceHash::LineMod, [5, 3, 3, 1], [6, 5, 3, 5]),
            (SliceHash::SectorMod, [2, 0, 0, 4], [3, 6, 5, 6]),
            (SliceHash::XorFolded, [5, 1, 2, 3], [6, 3, 4, 4]),
            (SliceHash::KnuthMult, [3, 1, 1, 1], [6, 5, 1, 6]),
            (SliceHash::ShiftMod, [5, 1, 1, 0], [6, 2, 1, 2]),
            (SliceHash::BitReverse, [3, 5, 5, 3], [1, 0, 3, 2]),
        ];
        for (hash, at6, at7) in cases {
            for (i, &line) in lines.iter().enumerate() {
                assert_eq!(hash.slice_of(line, 6), at6[i], "{hash:?}({line}, 6)");
                assert_eq!(hash.slice_of(line, 7), at7[i], "{hash:?}({line}, 7)");
            }
        }
        // Set mapping floors too: Python (-93 // 6) % 512 == 496.
        let mut l2 = L2Model::new(cfg(6_291_456, 16, 6)).unwrap();
        assert!(!rd(&mut l2, -93, 1), "cold negative line");
        assert!(rd(&mut l2, -93, 1), "tagged and re-hit, no wrap");
    }

    /// Pinned against Python `CacheReplayConfig` derived properties.
    #[test]
    fn geometry_derivation_matches_python() {
        let c = cfg(6_291_456, 16, 6);
        assert_eq!(c.total_lines(), 49_152);
        assert_eq!(c.num_sets_per_slice(), 512);
        // Tiny degenerate config exercises both max(1, ·) clamps.
        let tiny = cfg(1024, 16, 6);
        assert_eq!(tiny.total_lines(), 8);
        assert_eq!(tiny.num_sets_per_slice(), 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn carded_constructor_applies_documented_defaults() {
        let policy = Some(L2_WRITE_ALLOCATE_POLICY);
        let c = L2Config::from_carded_geometry("sm_86", 6_291_456, 128, 32, 6, policy).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(c.associativity, DOCUMENTED_DEFAULT_L2_ASSOCIATIVITY);
        assert_eq!(c.replacement, L2Replacement::Lru);
        assert_eq!(c.slice_hash, SliceHash::LineMod);
        assert!(matches!(
            L2Config::from_carded_geometry("sm_86", 6_291_456, 256, 32, 6, policy),
            Err(L2ConfigError::UnsupportedGranularity { .. })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            L2Config::from_carded_geometry("sm_86", 64, 128, 32, 6, policy),
            Err(L2ConfigError::CapacityBelowLine { .. })
        ));
    }

    /// Fail-closed gates on the carded constructor: an arch that never
    /// reviewed the documented defaults, and a card whose write policy
    /// is a gap (sm_120-laptop ships `policy: null`) or an unknown
    /// token, must all be typed errors — the store path write-allocates
    /// and must never assume it.
    #[test]
    fn carded_constructor_fails_closed_on_arch_and_policy() {
        let policy = Some(L2_WRITE_ALLOCATE_POLICY);
        assert!(matches!(
            L2Config::from_carded_geometry("sm_120", 33_554_432, 128, 32, 12, policy),
            Err(L2ConfigError::DefaultsUnreviewedForArch { .. })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            L2Config::from_carded_geometry("sm_86", 6_291_456, 128, 32, 6, None),
            Err(L2ConfigError::WritePolicyGap)
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            L2Config::from_carded_geometry("sm_86", 6_291_456, 128, 32, 6, Some("write_back")),
            Err(L2ConfigError::WritePolicyUnsupported { .. })
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn sector_hit_requires_line_and_sector() {
        let mut l2 = L2Model::new(cfg(1024, 2, 1)).unwrap();
        assert!(!rd(&mut l2, 0, 0), "cold line miss");
        assert!(rd(&mut l2, 0, 0), "sector now valid");
        assert!(!rd(&mut l2, 0, 1), "resident line, new sector");
        assert!(rd(&mut l2, 0, 1));
        assert_eq!(l2.counters.line_misses, 1);
        assert_eq!(l2.counters.sector_fill_misses, 1);
        assert_eq!(l2.counters.hits, 2);
        assert_eq!(l2.counters.total(), 4);
    }

    #[test]
    fn lru_evicts_least_recent_line() {
        // 1 slice, 1 set (capacity 256 B / 128 B line / assoc 2), LRU.
        let mut l2 = L2Model::new(cfg(256, 2, 1)).unwrap();
        rd(&mut l2, 0, 0);
        rd(&mut l2, 1, 0);
        rd(&mut l2, 0, 0); // line 0 → MRU
        rd(&mut l2, 2, 0); // evicts line 1
        assert!(rd(&mut l2, 0, 0), "line 0 survived");
        assert!(!rd(&mut l2, 1, 0), "line 1 was evicted");
    }

    #[test]
    fn eviction_drops_sector_residency_with_the_line() {
        let mut l2 = L2Model::new(cfg(128, 1, 1)).unwrap();
        rd(&mut l2, 0, 0);
        rd(&mut l2, 0, 1);
        rd(&mut l2, 9, 0); // same set (1 set total) → evict
        assert!(!rd(&mut l2, 0, 1), "sector died with the line");
        assert_eq!(l2.counters.line_misses, 3);
    }

    #[test]
    fn set_mapping_matches_python_form() {
        // 1 slice, 2 sets, assoc 1 (capacity 256, line 128, assoc 1):
        // lines 0 and 2 share set 0; line 1 lives in set 1.
        let mut l2 = L2Model::new(cfg(256, 1, 1)).unwrap();
        rd(&mut l2, 0, 0);
        rd(&mut l2, 1, 0);
        rd(&mut l2, 2, 0); // evicts line 0, not line 1
        assert!(rd(&mut l2, 1, 0), "set 1 undisturbed");
        assert!(!rd(&mut l2, 0, 0), "conflict-evicted");
    }

    #[test]
    fn srrip_ages_and_reinserts_at_long_interval() {
        let mut c = cfg(256, 2, 1);
        c.replacement = L2Replacement::Srrip;
        let mut l2 = L2Model::new(c).unwrap();
        rd(&mut l2, 0, 0); // insert rrpv=2
        rd(&mut l2, 2, 0); // insert rrpv=2 (same set)
        rd(&mut l2, 0, 0); // hit → rrpv=0
        // New line: no way at max → age all (0→1, 2→3), evict line 2.
        rd(&mut l2, 4, 0);
        assert!(rd(&mut l2, 0, 0), "recently-hit line survives");
        assert!(!rd(&mut l2, 2, 0), "aged line evicted");
    }

    #[test]
    fn bip_inserts_below_lru_except_periodically() {
        let mut c = cfg(256, 2, 1);
        c.replacement = L2Replacement::Bip;
        let mut l2 = L2Model::new(c).unwrap();
        // bip_counter=0 → first install at MRU; the next 31 at LRU-1.
        rd(&mut l2, 0, 0); // MRU insert (counter 0)
        rd(&mut l2, 2, 0); // below line 0 (counter 1)
        rd(&mut l2, 4, 0); // evicts line 2 (lowest recency)
        assert!(rd(&mut l2, 0, 0), "MRU-inserted line survives");
        assert!(!rd(&mut l2, 2, 0), "LRU-inserted line evicted");
    }

    /// Cross-language lockstep corpus (BL-20260507 pattern): the SAME
    /// deterministic LCG streams, replayed through the canonical Python
    /// engine, produce these (hits, total) pins —
    /// `tools/cache_replay/test_l2_rust_parity.py` asserts the Python
    /// side AND that these rows exist here. Regenerate BOTH files in
    /// one commit.
    #[test]
    fn python_parity_corpus_pins() {
        // (policy, hash, seed, capacity, assoc, slices, n, line_space,
        //  signed, hits, total)
        type Row = (
            L2Replacement,
            SliceHash,
            u64,
            u64,
            u32,
            u32,
            u64,
            i64,
            bool,
            u64,
            u64,
        );
        #[rustfmt::skip]
        let corpus: [Row; 7] = [
            (L2Replacement::Lru, SliceHash::LineMod, 1, 16384, 4, 3, 500, 128, false, 159, 500),
            (L2Replacement::Lru, SliceHash::KnuthMult, 2, 16384, 4, 3, 500, 128, false, 164, 500),
            (L2Replacement::Srrip, SliceHash::XorFolded, 3, 16384, 4, 3, 500, 128, false, 150, 500),
            (L2Replacement::Srrip, SliceHash::BitReverse, 4, 4096, 2, 2, 500, 256, false, 6, 500),
            (L2Replacement::Bip, SliceHash::SectorMod, 5, 16384, 4, 3, 500, 128, false, 181, 500),
            (L2Replacement::Bip, SliceHash::ShiftMod, 6, 4096, 2, 2, 500, 256, false, 11, 500),
            (L2Replacement::Lru, SliceHash::LineMod, 7, 4096, 2, 3, 400, 96, true, 14, 400),
        ];
        for (policy, hash, seed, cap, assoc, slices, n, space, signed, hits, total) in corpus {
            let mut l2 = L2Model::new(L2Config {
                capacity_bytes: cap,
                line_bytes: 128,
                sector_bytes: 32,
                num_slices: slices,
                associativity: assoc,
                replacement: policy,
                slice_hash: hash,
            })
            .unwrap();
            let mut x: u64 = seed;
            for _ in 0..n {
                x = x
                    .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
                    .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
                let mut line = ((x >> 20) % space as u64) as i64;
                if signed && (x & 1) == 1 {
                    line = -line;
                }
                rd(&mut l2, line, ((x >> 10) & 3) as u8);
            }
            assert_eq!(
                (l2.counters.hits, l2.counters.total()),
                (hits, total),
                "corpus row seed={seed} ({policy:?}, {hash:?})"
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn stores_allocate_like_loads() {
        let mut l2 = L2Model::new(cfg(1024, 2, 1)).unwrap();
        assert!(!wr(&mut l2, 3, 2), "cold store misses (no tag to match)");
        assert!(
            rd(&mut l2, 3, 2),
            "write-allocate: the store's line services a later load"
        );
        assert_eq!(l2.counters.line_misses, 1);
        assert_eq!(l2.counters.write_tag_hits, 0, "cold path grants no tag hit");
    }

    /// The §6.4 per-access-class rule: a write-class access to a
    /// RESIDENT line hits on the tag alone, even when the sector's
    /// valid bit is clear — and validates the sector (the write carries
    /// its own data), so a later read of that sector hits too. The same
    /// interleaving under Read class stays a sector-fill miss: the STATE
    /// trajectory is identical, only the counting differs.
    #[test]
    fn write_class_hits_on_tag_match_and_validates_the_sector() {
        let mut l2 = L2Model::new(cfg(1024, 2, 1)).unwrap();
        assert!(!wr(&mut l2, 3, 0), "cold write line-misses");
        assert!(
            wr(&mut l2, 3, 2),
            "write to a NEW sector of the resident line: tag-match hit"
        );
        assert_eq!(l2.counters.write_tag_hits, 1);
        assert_eq!(
            l2.counters.sector_fill_misses, 0,
            "the tag-match hit is not double-counted as a fill miss"
        );
        assert!(
            rd(&mut l2, 3, 2),
            "the write validated the sector — a later read hits"
        );
        // Physics stays honest for pricing: a tag-match hit to a fresh
        // sector reports it ABSENT before the access (an atomic reply
        // would still fetch from DRAM), while a re-read finds it present.
        let out = l2.access(3, 3, L2OpClass::WriteAtomic);
        assert!(out.counted_hit && !out.sector_present);
        let out = l2.access(3, 3, L2OpClass::Read);
        assert!(out.counted_hit && out.sector_present);
        // Mirror stream under Read class: same state, different counts.
        let mut r = L2Model::new(cfg(1024, 2, 1)).unwrap();
        assert!(!rd(&mut r, 3, 0));
        assert!(!rd(&mut r, 3, 2), "read of the invalid sector fill-misses");
        assert_eq!(r.counters.sector_fill_misses, 1);
        assert_eq!(r.counters.write_tag_hits, 0);
        assert!(rd(&mut r, 3, 2));
    }

    /// Tag-match never crosses an eviction: once the line is gone the
    /// write-class access line-misses like everyone else.
    #[test]
    fn write_class_tag_hit_dies_with_the_line() {
        let mut l2 = L2Model::new(cfg(128, 1, 1)).unwrap();
        assert!(!wr(&mut l2, 0, 0));
        assert!(!rd(&mut l2, 9, 0), "same single set → evicts line 0");
        assert!(!wr(&mut l2, 0, 1), "no resident tag, no write hit");
        assert_eq!(l2.counters.write_tag_hits, 0);
    }
}
```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Timing-specific accuracy runner for the cycle prediction bundle.

This scorer joins prediction rows to the scoped long-duration timing cohort on
a timing-only key: slug, shape_point, arch, binary identity, kernel signature,
source commit, and metric target. The cache-layer dimension is intentionally
absent because this target is elapsed cycles, not a per-cache-layer fraction.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import math
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Sequence


REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
if str(REPO_ROOT) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT))

from tools.local_labels import timing_prediction_contract as contract  # noqa: E402
from workloads.simbench_bw.timing_cycle_predictor import (  # noqa: E402
    DEMOTED_MODEL_VERSIONS,
    DEPLOYABLE_CHANNEL,
    DIAGNOSTIC_SAME_SLUG_CHANNEL,
)


DEFAULT_COHORT = (
    REPO_ROOT
    / "data"
    / "local_labels"
    / "timing_cohort"
    / "ac4_long_duration_cohort_sm_86.json"
)
DEFAULT_PREDICTIONS = (
    REPO_ROOT
    / "data"
    / "local_labels"
    / "timing_predictions"
    / "timing_cycle_predictions_sm_86.json"
)
DEFAULT_OUTPUT = (
    REPO_ROOT
    / "data"
    / "local_labels"
    / "timing_predictions"
    / "timing_accuracy_report_sm_86.json"
)

JOIN_KEY_FIELDS = (
    "slug",
    "shape_point",
    "arch",
    "binary_sha256",
    "kernel_signature_sha256",
    "source_commit",
    "metric_target",
)
FORBIDDEN_JOIN_FIELDS = ("cache_layer",)
METRIC_TARGET = "cycles"
RESAMPLE_SEED = 20260531


class TimingAccuracyError(ValueError):
    """Raised when predictions cannot be joined or scored."""


# Per-cell prediction-object keys that mark a same-slug / neighbor
# derivation. A deployable prediction carrying any of these is a
# diagnostic value masquerading as the headline and is rejected.
_SAME_SLUG_MARKER_FIELDS = (
    "channel",
    "neighbor_slug",
    "neighbor_shape_point",
    "neighbor_work_ratio",
)

# Value-level substitution tolerances. Marker fields are trivially
# strippable, so the guard rejects a deployable prediction whose
# NUMBERS sit in a forbidden proximity band around the demoted
# same-slug value. The band is SUBSTANTIVE, not exact-copy-sized: an
# epsilon-perturbed copy (x1.0001, x1.001, x1.01) is still a
# same-slug-derived headline and must be rejected. Calibration: the
# committed honest bundle's MINIMUM deployable-vs-diagnostic relative
# gap is ~2.417e-2 (pinned with headroom by
# test_committed_bundle_passes_value_substitution_audit); the band is
# a fixed 1e-2 — no larger than half the measured minimum gap, and
# wide enough that any disguise tighter than 1% relative is caught.
# This arm is the LOAD-BEARING rejection and is independent of the
# stored per-cell error field. The abs-log-error arm additionally
# catches a forged stored error equal to the diagnostic's.
_SAME_SLUG_VALUE_REL_TOLERANCE = 1e-2
_SAME_SLUG_ERROR_ABS_TOLERANCE = 1e-12


def assert_prediction_bundle_deployable_channel(
    predictions: dict[str, Any],
) -> None:
    """Fail-closed pre-scoring guard: the scored bundle must be the
    demotion-aware deployable ridge-on-roofline channel.

    Rejects (typed reasons in the message):
      - a bundle or cell whose model_version is a demoted
        same-slug-substitution version;
      - a bundle missing the deployable-channel declaration, the
        demoted-channels declaration, or the typed cohort-diversity
        limitation block;
      - a cell whose prediction_channel is not the deployable channel
        (e.g. the demoted diagnostic channel promoted to headline);
      - a cell missing the demoted same-slug diagnostics block this
        guard audits, or whose non-null diagnostic does not carry the
        diagnostic channel marker;
      - a deployable prediction object carrying same-slug/neighbor
        marker fields;
      - VALUE-level substitution: a deployable predicted_cycles equal
        (within tolerance) to the demoted diagnostic value, or a
        cell-level validation_abs_log_error equal to the diagnostic's
        (the rounded-value disguise) — markers are strippable, the
        numbers are the contraband.
    """
    model_version = predictions.get("model_version")
    if model_version in DEMOTED_MODEL_VERSIONS:
        raise TimingAccuracyError(
            "prediction_bundle_demoted_model_version: refusing to score "
            f"bundle model_version={model_version!r}; its deployable "
            "headline substitutes same-slug truth labels."
        )
    if predictions.get("deployable_channel") != DEPLOYABLE_CHANNEL:
        raise TimingAccuracyError(
            "prediction_bundle_channel_declaration_missing: the bundle "
            f"must declare deployable_channel={DEPLOYABLE_CHANNEL!r}; "
            f"got {predictions.get('deployable_channel')!r}."
        )
    demoted_channels = predictions.get("demoted_channels") or []
    if DIAGNOSTIC_SAME_SLUG_CHANNEL not in demoted_channels:
        raise TimingAccuracyError(
            "prediction_bundle_demoted_channels_missing: the bundle "
            f"must declare {DIAGNOSTIC_SAME_SLUG_CHANNEL!r} in "
            "demoted_channels so the value-substitution audit below "
            "has the diagnostic channel to compare against."
        )
    limitation = predictions.get("cohort_limitation")
    if (
        not isinstance(limitation, dict)
        or not limitation.get("typed_reason")
        or limitation.get("same_slug_substitution_authorized") is not False
    ):
        raise TimingAccuracyError(
            "prediction_bundle_demotion_limitation_missing: the bundle "
            "must carry the typed cohort_limitation block with "
            "same_slug_substitution_authorized=false."
        )
    for row in predictions.get("cells", []):
        cell_id = f"{row.get('slug')}/{row.get('shape_point')}"
        if row.get("model_version") in DEMOTED_MODEL_VERSIONS:
            raise TimingAccuracyError(
                "prediction_cell_demoted_model_version: cell "
                f"{cell_id} carries a demoted model_version."
            )
        channel = row.get("prediction_channel")
        if channel != DEPLOYABLE_CHANNEL:
            raise TimingAccuracyError(
                "prediction_cell_channel_not_deployable: cell "
                f"{cell_id} declares prediction_channel={channel!r} "
                f"(diagnostic channels such as "
                f"{DIAGNOSTIC_SAME_SLUG_CHANNEL!r} cannot be scored)."
            )
        markers = sorted(
            set(_SAME_SLUG_MARKER_FIELDS).intersection(
                row.get("prediction", {})
            )
        )
        if markers:
            raise TimingAccuracyError(
                "prediction_cell_same_slug_sourced: cell "
                f"{cell_id} deployable prediction carries same-slug "
                f"marker fields {markers}."
            )
        diagnostics = row.get("diagnostics")
        if (
            not isinstance(diagnostics, dict)
            or "same_slug_scaled_neighbor" not in diagnostics
        ):
            raise TimingAccuracyError(
                "prediction_cell_diagnostics_block_missing: cell "
                f"{cell_id} lacks the demoted same-slug diagnostics "
                "block the value-substitution audit requires."
            )
        diag = diagnostics["same_slug_scaled_neighbor"]
        if diag is None:
            continue
        if diag.get("channel") != DIAGNOSTIC_SAME_SLUG_CHANNEL:
            raise TimingAccuracyError(
                "prediction_cell_diagnostic_channel_mismatch: cell "
                f"{cell_id} diagnostic carries channel="
                f"{diag.get('channel')!r}; expected "
                f"{DIAGNOSTIC_SAME_SLUG_CHANNEL!r}."
            )
        # VALUE-level substitution audit: marker fields are trivially
        # strippable, so compare the numbers themselves. A deployable
        # prediction equal to the demoted same-slug value (within
        # tolerance) IS the retired v3 headline wearing v4 clothes.
        deploy_predicted = float(row["prediction"]["predicted_cycles"])
        diag_predicted = float(diag["predicted_cycles"])
        rel_gap = abs(deploy_predicted - diag_predicted) / max(
            abs(diag_predicted), 1.0
        )
        if rel_gap <= _SAME_SLUG_VALUE_REL_TOLERANCE:
            raise TimingAccuracyError(
                "prediction_cell_same_slug_value_substitution: cell "
                f"{cell_id} deployable predicted_cycles "
                f"{deploy_predicted!r} equals the demoted same-slug "
                f"diagnostic value {diag_predicted!r} within relative "
                f"tolerance {_SAME_SLUG_VALUE_REL_TOLERANCE}; the "
                "deployable headline may not be computed by same-slug "
                "substitution."
            )
        cell_err = row.get("validation_abs_log_error")
        diag_err = diag.get("validation_abs_log_error")
        if (
            cell_err is not None
            and diag_err is not None
            and abs(float(cell_err) - float(diag_err))
            <= _SAME_SLUG_ERROR_ABS_TOLERANCE
        ):
            raise TimingAccuracyError(
                "prediction_cell_same_slug_value_substitution: cell "
                f"{cell_id} cell-level validation_abs_log_error "
                f"{cell_err!r} equals the demoted diagnostic's "
                f"{diag_err!r} (rounded-value disguise); the "
                "deployable headline may not be computed by same-slug "
                "substitution."
            )


def _load_json(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def _repo_rel(path: Path) -> str:
    return str(path.resolve().relative_to(REPO_ROOT))


def _source_commit() -> str:
    try:
        return (
            subprocess.check_output(
                ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=str(REPO_ROOT), text=True
            )
            .strip()
        )
    except Exception:
        return "unknown"


def join_key_for_label(cell: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, str]:
    return {
        "slug": cell["slug"],
        "shape_point": cell["shape_point"],
        "arch": cell["arch"],
        "binary_sha256": cell["binary_sha256"],
        "kernel_signature_sha256": cell["kernel_signature_sha256"],
        "source_commit": cell["source_commit"],
        "metric_target": METRIC_TARGET,
    }


def _assert_timing_join_key(join_key: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    unexpected = set(join_key) - set(JOIN_KEY_FIELDS)
    missing = set(JOIN_KEY_FIELDS) - set(join_key)
    forbidden = set(FORBIDDEN_JOIN_FIELDS).intersection(join_key)
    if unexpected or missing or forbidden:
        raise TimingAccuracyError(
            "invalid timing join key: "
            f"unexpected={sorted(unexpected)}, missing={sorted(missing)}, "
            f"forbidden={sorted(forbidden)}"
        )


def _prediction_lookup(predictions: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[tuple[Any, ...], dict[str, Any]]:
    lookup: dict[tuple[Any, ...], dict[str, Any]] = {}
    for row in predictions.get("cells", []):
        join_key = row.get("join_key", {})
        _assert_timing_join_key(join_key)
        key = tuple(join_key[field] for field in JOIN_KEY_FIELDS)
        if key in lookup:
            raise TimingAccuracyError(f"duplicate prediction join key: {key!r}")
        lookup[key] = row
    return lookup


def joined_scored_cells(
    predictions: dict[str, Any], cohort: dict[str, Any]
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    lookup = _prediction_lookup(predictions)
    scored: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for label_cell in cohort.get("cells", []):
        join_key = join_key_for_label(label_cell)
        key = tuple(join_key[field] for field in JOIN_KEY_FIELDS)
        pred_cell = lookup.get(key)
        if pred_cell is None:
            raise TimingAccuracyError(f"missing prediction for timing key: {key!r}")
        predicted = float(pred_cell["prediction"]["predicted_cycles"])
        observed = float(label_cell["labels"]["gpc__cycles_elapsed.max"]["value"])
        if predicted <= 0.0 or observed <= 0.0:
            raise TimingAccuracyError("cycle predictions and labels must be positive")
        scored.append(
            {
                "slug": label_cell["slug"],
                "shape_point": label_cell["shape_point"],
                "arch": label_cell["arch"],
                "regime": pred_cell.get("regime", "long"),
                "join_key": join_key,
                "predicted_cycles": predicted,
                "observed_cycles": observed,
                "signed_log_ratio": math.log(predicted / observed),
            }
        )
    return scored


def _coverage_block(doc: dict[str, Any], n_scored: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
    gate = contract.publication_gate(doc)
    smoke = contract.smoke_tier(doc)
    return {
        "n_scored": n_scored,
        "publication_min_scored_cells": gate["min_scored_cells"],
        "smoke_min_scored_cells": smoke["min_scored_cells"],
        "publication_floor_met": n_scored >= gate["min_scored_cells"],
        "smoke_floor_met": n_scored >= smoke["min_scored_cells"],
    }


def build_accuracy_report_from_objects(
    *,
    predictions: dict[str, Any],
    cohort: dict[str, Any],
    contract_doc: dict[str, Any],
    prediction_path: Path = DEFAULT_PREDICTIONS,
    cohort_path: Path = DEFAULT_COHORT,
    source_commit: str | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    assert_prediction_bundle_deployable_channel(predictions)
    scored_cells = joined_scored_cells(predictions, cohort)
    pairs = [
        (cell["predicted_cycles"], cell["observed_cycles"]) for cell in scored_cells
    ]
    gate_cfg = contract.publication_gate(contract_doc)
    scores = contract.score_cycle_metrics(
        pairs,
        resamples=gate_cfg["bootstrap_resamples"],
        confidence=gate_cfg["bootstrap_ci_confidence"],
        seed=RESAMPLE_SEED,
    )
    gate = contract.evaluate_publication_gate(contract_doc, scores)
    coverage = _coverage_block(contract_doc, len(scored_cells))
    result_kind = "publication_pass" if gate["passes"] else "typed_unavailable"
    typed_reason = None if gate["passes"] else "cycle_publication_gate_not_met"
    return {
        "schema_version": 1,
        "artifact_kind": "timing_accuracy_report",
        "arch": cohort["arch"],
        "source_commit": source_commit or _source_commit(),
        "metric_target": METRIC_TARGET,
        "prediction_mode": "leave_one_out_validation",
        "scored_channel": DEPLOYABLE_CHANNEL,
        "demoted_channels_present": list(
            predictions.get("demoted_channels", [])
        ),
        "prediction_model_version": predictions.get("model_version"),
        "prediction_bundle": _repo_rel(prediction_path),
        "cohort_artifact": _repo_rel(cohort_path),
        "scoring_method": contract.PINNED_CYCLE_ERROR_METHOD,
        "join_key_fields": list(JOIN_KEY_FIELDS),
        "forbidden_join_fields": list(FORBIDDEN_JOIN_FIELDS),
        "bootstrap": {
            "resamples": gate_cfg["bootstrap_resamples"],
            "ci_confidence": gate_cfg["bootstrap_ci_confidence"],
            "seed": RESAMPLE_SEED,
        },
        "coverage": coverage,
        "scores": scores,
        "publication_gate": gate,
        "result_kind": result_kind,
        "typed_unavailable_reason": typed_reason,
        "evidence_status": "Offline-verified",
        "cells": scored_cells,
    }


def build_accuracy_report(
    *,
    prediction_path: Path = DEFAULT_PREDICTIONS,
    cohort_path: Path = DEFAULT_COHORT,
    contract_path: Path = contract.DEFAULT_CONTRACT_PATH,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    predictions = _load_json(prediction_path)
    cohort = _load_json(cohort_path)
    doc = contract.load_contract(contract_path)
    return build_accuracy_report_from_objects(
        predictions=predictions,
        cohort=cohort,
        contract_doc=doc,
        prediction_path=prediction_path,
        cohort_path=cohort_path,
    )


def write_report(report: dict[str, Any], output: Path) -> None:
    output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    output.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--predictions", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_PREDICTIONS)
    parser.add_argument("--cohort", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_COHORT)
    parser.add_argument("--contract", type=Path, default=contract.DEFAULT_CONTRACT_PATH)
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_OUTPUT)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    report = build_accuracy_report(
        prediction_path=args.predictions,
        cohort_path=args.cohort,
        contract_path=args.contract,
    )
    write_report(report, args.output)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```
